The travel montage continues through a variety of vacation scenes. A dark-haired man in a suit appears indoors, followed by passengers seated inside an airplane, including a young woman by a window and a man behind her. Two people ride horses along a grassy ridge with blue mountains in the distance. A man in white tennis clothes swings a racket on an outdoor court bordered by glass and dark fencing. A blonde woman in a yellow top and white skirt swings a golf club while a man stands nearby watching among trees and palms. Inside an airplane galley, a young female flight attendant with short dark hair and a United scarf pours or serves from a silver coffee pot, then brings a tray with cups to seated passengers, including an older man who smiles and reaches toward it. Outdoors again, an older couple walks between rocky cliffs; another couple sits back-to-back in a small blue boat on calm water; and a lone kayaker in dark clothing paddles through churning whitewater rapids. The Golden Gate Bridge stretches across blue water in another destination view. Families and leisure travel appear as well. In an airplane cabin, a man in glasses sits by the window holding a cup, while a child nearby holds an orange “Come fly with me...” balloon; another passenger leans over to point out the window. A family rides in an open-top car, with children in the back holding red, blue, and white balloons. A castle-like entrance, resembling a theme-park castle, stands against a bright blue sky as an old-fashioned car passes in front. In another interior, a family group is silhouetted near tall columns, then the Lincoln Memorial statue is seen from below, seated high on its pedestal. Throughout these scenes, round buttons and balloons repeat the “Come fly with me...” lettering, tying the travelers and United staff together visually. The final portion returns to United employees and slogan graphics. A white button with blue script reading “Come fly with me...” fills the screen, then dissolves into a smiling female attendant in a white cap. A young man in a dark suit stands beside red and blue balloons and reaches toward them. A male United employee in a light blue shirt and cap, wearing a tie and a round button, smiles in a modern terminal-like space. Three female flight attendants walk together down a bright corridor, each in a neat 1960s uniform and cap, carrying balloons in red, blue, and white; one wears white with dark trim, one wears dark with white trim, and one wears orange with white trim. Large words then appear one at a time across soft, colorful backgrounds: “Come,” then a stylized “fly,” then “with,” then “me...” The phrase resolves into the United slogan “fly the friendly skies of United” in large white decorative lettering. Behind the final slogan, a United jet climbs through a blue sky, angled upward, with its wing and engines visible as the aircraft continues into the clouds.

A silver-haired older woman identified by on-screen text as “Martha Raye denture wearer” walks onto a studio set. She has a bright, broad smile and wears a loose lavender tunic over white pants, with a white necklace or trim at the neckline. She stands beside a wide mirror bordered with round glowing bulbs. Her reflection appears in the mirror on the left, while the real figure stands on the right. The counter is cluttered with dressing-room items, including boxes, small containers, and a vase of red flowers. She turns toward the viewer, smiles, and picks up a small teal-green box from the vanity. Holding the box beside her face, she presents it clearly. Her fingers grip the sides of the box, and the lavender of her outfit is blurred behind it. She then appears again in the dressing room, smiling while holding the Polident box up near her cheek. The commercial moves into a product demonstration. A hand holds a set of dentures against a dark background. The teeth and gum line are visibly marked with heavy brownish stains, especially along and between the teeth. The stained dentures are lowered into a clear cylindrical glass. White lettering on the glass reads “Extra Strength Polident.” The dentures sit at the bottom in liquid. A hand drops a tablet into the glass, and white-blue foam begins to bloom and swirl around the dentures. The liquid becomes cloudy and effervescent, filling much of the glass with cleaning action. White on-screen text appears near the bottom: “15 minutes later.” A hand reaches into the glass and lifts out the dentures, now appearing bright white. In a close view, two hands hold the cleaned denture sections apart, showing smooth white surfaces and clean spaces between the teeth, with the earlier brown staining no longer visible. The “15 minutes later” text remains at the bottom during this reveal. The scene returns to the dressing room. Martha Raye stands in front of the lit vanity mirror, smiling broadly in her lavender outfit, with the flowers and dressing-table objects still behind her. She speaks toward the viewer, then raises the teal Polident box beside her face again. White on-screen text appears across the lower part of the image: “Polident green gets tough stains clean.” She holds the product steady near her cheek, alternating between a knowing look and a big smile, keeping the package label visible as the commercial ends.

The gloved hand grasps the box and brings it forward. As more people come into view, the line looks like a broad cross-section of the town, all standing close together and calmly presenting the product. An adult man with light skin and neatly combed brown hair faces forward outdoors, with dark green wooded hills behind him. A dramatic image follows of a TWA jet flying past a grid of tall building windows against a vivid orange-red sky, the plane’s red tail clearly visible as it crosses the glassy urban backdrop. Another passenger reclines deeply in a seat by the windows, head tilted back, appearing restful. The elderly woman with white hair appears again, smiling softly while holding a small item in her hands, comfortable in her seat. The Black female staff member returns in close view, smiling with a red scarf at her collar, with a busy but softly blurred service area behind her. The headset-wearing employees at terminals appear again, three in a row, all focused on their screens and microphones. Centered across the sky in white capital letters is the on-screen slogan: “LEADING THE WAY. TWA.” The plane continues along the lower left beneath the text, set against the deep blue, red, and gold colors of the horizon.

A Texaco gas station sits beyond a wide, divided roadway in a dry, open landscape under warm, late-day light. In the nearer foreground are gas pumps marked “ZX,” with cars parked among them, including a white coupe. He looks down and around the pump area, then straightens up, his expression shifting into a faint, self-satisfied or knowing smile. Behind him, large red “ZX” letters are visible on the station wall. He looks across the forecourt with a cautious, alert expression, as if noticing the Texaco station in the distance. He then climbs out of the car and heads away from it toward the divided roadway. The man in the pale shirt crosses the broad, empty road on foot. From a high, wide view, the road stretches far into the horizon, split by a long central barrier. He walks across one side of the pavement, steps over or around the center divider, and continues toward the opposite side, visually turning the phrase “going the extra mile” into a literal journey across a huge span of road. Back at the pump area, the balding man stands by his car and pump, watching with a slightly puzzled, stern, or skeptical look. The “ZX” pump and the large red “Z” lettering remain behind him. The younger man is now at a Texaco pump. The pump has black panels, red and white Texaco branding, and the Texaco star emblem on a red lower section. He reaches for a nozzle, lifting it from the pump, then looks off to the side as if checking the distance back to his car. A later wide view shows him near the center divider again, holding the gas nozzle, with a long black hose stretching away across the pavement. Returning to the white coupe, he opens the car’s fuel door and brings the nozzle to the gas tank. He stands beside the rear quarter panel, one hand holding the fuel door open and the other guiding the nozzle into place. The hose trails from his hand back out of view, implying it has been stretched all the way from the Texaco pump. In the background, the balding man and the ZX pumps are still nearby, contrasting with the Texaco source of the fuel. After fueling, the younger man stands at a service window or cashier counter. Behind the glass is a blonde woman, likely a station attendant, wearing a black-and-white striped Texaco shirt with the red star logo on the chest. Shelves behind her hold bottles, containers, and convenience-store items. She turns toward him, smiles, and hands him small items or paperwork through the window. He reaches in to receive them. Their exchange is friendly and efficient, with the clerk smiling as she completes the transaction. The commercial returns to the wide exterior view. The Texaco station and its red-letter sign are again visible across the broad roadway. In the foreground, the balding man is beside a pump and car; he looks toward the Texaco station in the distance. He then turns and starts walking away from the pump area in that direction, leaving the pump behind as the Texaco sign remains prominent across the road.

LOUIS” and “BANK.” Small triangular indicator lights sit beside several buttons. The shapes look like parts of a television cabinet or screen housing being constructed in space. Rectangular frames rotate and align; one large box-like outline sits forward, with smaller rectangular forms moving toward it. The lines are bright electric blue-white, with a halo of light around them. Pieces appear to assemble around a central rectangular opening, suggesting the body of a television set forming from individual panels. More components move into position. Her knees bend easily as she lowers herself, and she keeps one hand near her skirt while offering food with the other. Next, she moves to a bench near flower beds and sits down. The commercial opens in a very dark, greenish view of a car shape, then brightens to a clear exterior view of a glossy red four-door sedan parked on a pale gravel driveway. The car is positioned in front of a large, old-looking brick house with arched doorways, steep rooflines, and dense green shrubs. Its long hood, squared-off body, chrome trim, and silver wheels are shown in profile, with the front angled slightly toward the viewer. A close view moves to the red driver’s-side door. A light-skinned hand and forearm, wearing a brown tweed or wool jacket with a light shirt cuff and wristwatch, reaches for the chrome door handle. The hand pulls the handle, and the red door swings open, revealing a warm tan interior. The front seats are broad and cushioned, upholstered in tan and cream tones with vertical stitched panels and darker piping. The driver’s seat and passenger seat sit side by side, with a black steering wheel and center console visible toward the left. Inside the car, the dashboard and steering wheel are shown from the driver’s position. The black steering wheel has the Audi four-ring emblem at its center, and behind it is a dark instrument cluster with round gauges. Greenery outside the windshield suggests the car is still near the landscaped driveway. A person, visible mostly from behind and by their hands, sits in the driver’s seat wearing the same brown jacket. Their hands settle on the steering wheel, suggesting readiness to drive. The view shifts upward to the car’s ceiling. A hand reaches to a small overhead control near the front of the roof liner. A rectangular sunroof opening is visible above, with tree branches and bright sunlight beyond it. As the roof opening is shown, a bright flare of sun shines through the trees, making the sunroof feel airy and open. The center console is then shown in close detail. It contains a black and silver automatic gear selector set in a curved track, with small white position markers along one side. The driver’s hand reaches in and moves the slim gear lever through the gate, emphasizing the car’s controls and interior finish. The exterior side windows reveal the tan cabin again, with the front and rear seats visible through the red door frames and chrome window trim. The upholstery appears plush and roomy, with matching tan door panels and armrests. The view passes along the side of the car from the front seating area toward the rear, showing the back seat’s broad cushions and headrests through slightly reflective glass. The perspective changes to inside the moving car, looking out through the windshield over the dashboard. The driver is seen from behind on the left, hands on the steering wheel. Ahead, the car travels along a narrow mountain road carved into a rocky hillside. A steep rock wall rises close on the right, while the left side opens to a wide green valley below. The windshield frames the road as it curves along the cliff, with the rearview mirror hanging at the top center and the hood edge barely visible at the bottom. The driver’s hands adjust gently on the wheel as the road bends, while the scenery outside alternates between rocky cliff face, roadside greenery, and distant rolling landscape. The drive transitions back toward a residential setting. Through the windshield, the view returns to a leafy driveway bordered by hedges and brick walls. The red sedan then appears from the left side of the screen, rolling across the pale driveway in front of the same lush garden and brick house. As it comes fully into view, large white text appears above the car: “PORSCHE + AUDI.” Beneath it, in smaller white capital letters, the slogan reads, “NOTHING EVEN COMES CLOSE.” The red sedan remains displayed below the text, cleanly presented against the green hedges and stately home backdrop.

The commercial opens outdoors in a sunny park beside a bright yellow M&M’s candy cart. The cart has a yellow-and-dark-striped awning, large spoked wheels, and black “m&m’s” lettering on its side. Next to it stands a smiling young adult dressed like a cheerful vendor or candy maker, wearing a black turtleneck, a yellow apron with “m&m” printed on it, yellow suspenders, and a cap. Behind the cart are green lawns and trees, giving the scene a playful fairground feeling. A group of children, teenagers, and young adults in coordinated yellow, brown, orange, and white outfits run toward the cart across the grass. Their clothes have a 1970s look: flared pants, sporty shorts, tall socks, caps, vests, and shirts with M&M-style emblems. Several carry bowls or containers, and they gather together with excited faces, moving in a loose cluster as if they are the “M&M’s Candies Gang” mentioned in the audio context. A small child with a round afro wears a yellow shirt; another child in white overalls and a yellow cap carries a bowl; a blonde girl in yellow shorts and white knee socks moves near the front; older teens and young adults flank them in yellow jackets, brown tops, and cream-colored pants. The group crowds around a candy-making machine built into the cart. On top are metal bowls and funnels connected by a shiny pipe-like fixture. Close up, two large bowls are shown: one filled with small pale pieces that look like peanuts, and the other filled with dark chocolate pieces or chips. Hands use scoops to pour the pale peanuts and dark chocolate into separate metal funnels. Faces smile behind the machine as the ingredients slide down, visually matching the audio’s references to peanuts, chocolate, and mixing them together. The front of the machine shows a large black “m&m’s” logo with the words “PLAIN AND PEANUT CHOCOLATE CANDIES” underneath. Above the logo is a row of rectangular windows. At first the windows are blank white, then colored panels appear one by one, filling the row with bright green, orange, dark brown or black, yellow, and brown tones. The visual suggests the candies are being given their rainbow colors. The machine then reveals two lower openings labeled “PEANUT” on the left and “PLAIN” on the right. Hands hold branded M&M’s packages beneath the openings: a yellow package under “PEANUT” and a brown package under “PLAIN.” Small colorful candies pour out into the packages and into a copper-colored bowl, showing the product being made and packed. The group then appears gathered closely around the machine and cart, smiling and leaning in from all sides. The child in white overalls sits high on someone’s shoulder near the right, while others crowd around the top of the cart and look toward the machine. The mood is busy and festive, with everyone dressed in the brand’s yellow and brown palette. The scene shifts to a wider view in the park by a large fountain. The gang stands in a line along the fountain’s edge, with water spraying high on the left and trees and grass behind them. They step and sway together in a simple coordinated dance, then move closer and pose with hands on hips. Their outfits remain bright and coordinated: yellow sweatshirts and jackets, brown shirts, orange vests, white pants, and striped socks. The child in white overalls and yellow cap stands at one end, while the smaller child in the yellow shirt stands nearby. The group faces forward like a team proudly presenting themselves. The yellow M&M’s cart reappears near the fountain, its striped canopy and big wheels prominent. Several children and teens dance and jog around it. The small child in the yellow shirt moves near the cart’s wheel; the child in white overalls skips past; another girl in an orange vest bounces along with an arm raised. Older members stand by the cart handles and sides, smiling and reacting as the younger ones circle around. Baskets or containers sit on the cart’s counter beneath the awning, and the large black “m&m’s” logo is visible on the side panel. The fountain’s white spray rises behind the cart, making a bright backdrop as the group keeps moving around it. For the ending, everyone gathers tightly in a close group outdoors, filling the picture. At the center is the young adult in the black turtleneck and yellow suspenders, wearing a cap and holding M&M’s candies near his mouth. Around him, the children and teens hold M&M’s packages in yellow, brown, and orange wrappers, some with the bold “m&m’s” logo clearly visible. Several are eating the candies, raising pieces to their mouths, smiling, and looking toward the center or outward. The group is packed shoulder to shoulder, affectionate and lively, with arms around one another and faces turned up toward the central figure. White on-screen text appears along the bottom with the familiar slogan: “The milk chocolate melts in your mouth— not in your hand.” The group continues chewing, smiling, and holding up the candy packages as the commercial closes with the fountain still visible behind them.

A glamorous, fair-skinned woman with short, voluminous copper-blonde hair sits in a dim dressing-room-like setting beside a mirror edged with round glowing bulbs. Dark greenery and pale flowers fill the background, giving the space a staged, theatrical feel. She wears a loose rust-brown robe or dress with a low neckline, earrings, and pronounced eye makeup. At first she is seen mainly through the mirror, touching the side of her neck or hair with one hand, then smiling broadly as she looks toward her reflection and the viewer. Her real profile appears at the left edge while her reflected face remains to the right. White on-screen text identifies her as “Juliet Prowse.” She turns away from the mirror, still smiling, and shifts forward and out of the seated pose. The view changes to a close look at her legs stretched out horizontally against a dark background. She is wearing sheer pantyhose and delicate strappy high-heeled sandals. One leg rests above the other, with the ankle and lower calf clearly visible; the pantyhose lie smooth against the skin. Her hand hovers above and gestures near the ankle area, drawing attention to the fit around the ankle. She then appears again from the waist up in the same dark, floral dressing-room setting. She looks down briefly, then lifts a small egg-shaped package beside her face. The package is white with a blue band and the Leggs name on it. Holding it upright in one hand, she presents it toward the viewer while speaking, smiling at moments and keeping the product near her cheek so the label is easy to see. A plain beige title card follows. In large red serif capital letters centered on the screen, it reads “MEMORY YARN.” Small copyright text appears at the lower left, including “© 1978 Leggs Products.” The words remain on screen for several moments, emphasizing the product feature named in the audio context. The commercial ends with a product display against a dark background and pale floor. A large white Leggs egg package stands upright, the blue “Leggs” logo printed on the top half. The egg is open in the middle, with the top and bottom separated like a hinged container. Through the rectangular opening, a pair of smooth pantyhosed legs in strappy heels is visible, posed elegantly inside the package. The legs withdraw or disappear as the egg closes into a complete oval. The final image shows the closed white Leggs egg above black on-screen text reading, “Nothing beats a great pair of Leggs.”

A leafy outdoor path appears in a sunny residential or park-like setting, with shrubs, grass, and trees casting shade. Beside the path is a large rectangular street sign mounted on a gray post. The sign has a pale yellow face with a black border and bold black lettering that reads “PLEASANT” over smaller “STREET.” A light-skinned adult woman with a short blonde-brown bob walks along the path beneath the sign. She wears a light plaid button-up shirt and light-colored pants. As she comes closer, her face looks strained and uncomfortable. She suddenly opens her mouth as if about to sneeze, then lifts a white tissue to her nose and mouth with both hands. Her eyes squeeze shut, her head dips forward, and she hunches slightly over the tissue, showing the discomfort of hay fever or a cold. The view returns to the street sign, and the words on it change from “PLEASANT STREET” to “HAYFEVER STREET,” keeping the same sign shape, colors, and post but replacing the friendly name with the illness-related one. The commercial then shows the product package by itself against a plain light background. It is a rectangular Dristan box with a brown-orange top panel and white lower panel. Large white letters on the brown-orange panel read “DRISTAN,” with “DECONGESTANT TABLETS” underneath. The white area below includes the visible wording “SYMPTOMATIC RELIEF OF COLDS & HAY FEVER SINUS CONGESTION.” Next, several medicines are displayed on a clean white surface for comparison. On the left lies a red transparent capsule with many tiny pink-and-white beads inside. Behind it is a long pale beige oblong tablet or capsule shape, and in front is a flat round blue tablet. A separate round yellow tablet appears to the right, set apart from the others, with the label “DRISTAN” printed below it in black. The words “EXTRA MEDICINE” then appear above and near the Dristan tablet, visually emphasizing that the yellow Dristan tablet has something additional compared with the other medicine forms. The scene returns outdoors to the same woman in a green yard with trees and bushes. She is now crouched beside a medium-to-large dark brown dog with floppy ears. White on-screen text at the bottom reads “USE ONLY AS DIRECTED.” The woman bends down affectionately, putting her arms around the dog and holding its collar or leash. Her expression is now cheerful and relaxed. She hugs the dog close, smiling broadly, while the dog faces to the side calmly. The lawn and shrubbery behind them are sunlit, and the woman appears comfortable and active again. The “HAYFEVER STREET” sign appears once more on its gray post, still in the leafy outdoor setting. Then the sign changes into a product-style sign for Dristan, using the same suspended sign position. It shows the Dristan package design with the visible words “DRISTAN,” “DECONGESTANT TABLETS,” “COLDS & HAY FEVER,” and “SINUS CONGESTION.” Across the lower part of the screen, large white capital letters read, “EXTRA RELIEF MEDICINE THE OTHERS DON’T HAVE.” In the background near the path, the woman and her dark dog pass by, reinforcing the image of her being well enough to be outside and moving comfortably again.

The commercial opens on a black background with a bright, decorative title card. In glowing pink and orange lettering, surrounded by a flower-like retro border, the words “Once Upon a Time” appear. The scene changes to a small, theatrical boutique display packed with mannequins, clothing, accessories, shiny shelves, and hanging globe lights. The lighting is saturated and dreamlike, with deep black shadows and washes of hot pink, blue, green, and purple. In the center foreground sits a feminine mannequin dressed entirely in pink: a soft pink dress with long sleeves, large round pink sunglasses, curly pink hair or wig styled in bunches at the sides, and long necklaces hanging over her chest. Her face has a doll-like, fixed expression, with a small open mouth and decorative spots or flowers on the cheeks. Around her are other mannequin figures: to the left, a blue mannequin in a hooded blue outfit with a dramatic necklace and one arm raised; to the right, a green mannequin in flowing green clothing with a veil or long scarf over the head, a large black star painted over one eye, and an arm lifted as if posed mid-dance. Behind them are more fashion display figures and hanging lights, including a pale mannequin head in sunglasses. A dark-haired, adult feminine figure in a yellow or gold outfit moves among the displays behind the pink mannequin. She wears a sleeveless or short-sleeved yellow garment with a matching scarf or vest, and her dark hair is styled in a rounded bob. She leans toward the seated pink mannequin, looking down near the mannequin’s arm and wrist, as if noticing what is missing from the outfit. The pink mannequin remains seated with both arms slightly lifted, palms open, her sunglasses catching the colored light. A close view of her face emphasizes her oversized glasses, curled pink hair, and blank, sad-looking doll expression. The yellow-clad figure then turns toward the green mannequin, who stands partly hidden by a blue vertical panel and reflective shop fixtures. The green mannequin’s face, with the star over one eye and scattered small dots, is shown more closely under bright globe lights. She wears a head covering or veil that drapes down the sides of her face, and long strands or beads hang over her chest. The mood remains like a fashionable, nighttime window display. Attention shifts to the blue mannequin on the left. She is posed in a flowing blue outfit, with one arm bent above her head and the other hand at her waist. Large layered necklaces hang down the front of the garment. The yellow-clad figure moves nearby and gestures toward the blue mannequin’s wrist area, again drawing attention to the absence of a watch. The boutique set is dense with props: chrome poles, small shelves, colorful purses, hats, jewelry, and bright plastic-looking accessories. Back in the central display, the pink mannequin sits with the yellow-clad figure standing behind her. The yellow figure gestures and then moves away toward the left side of the boutique. The pink mannequin turns her head, still wearing her round sunglasses, as if becoming alert. The display becomes a still, balanced tableau again: the blue mannequin on the left, the pink mannequin at center, and the green mannequin on the right beneath glowing hanging lights. Then the mannequins appear to come to life. The pink mannequin shifts from her seated pose, lowers her arms, and begins moving through the display. The green mannequin on the right leans and raises an arm, her flowing sleeve and veil catching the green and magenta light. The figures seem to awaken within the shop window, moving carefully among the shelves and hanging lamps. The pink mannequin stands in her short pink dress, one hand resting near a small round table or shelf beside her. She turns toward a display of accessories. In profile, her curled pink hair, sunglasses, and long necklace are visible beneath bright globe bulbs. She brings a hand up near her face as if thinking, then looks toward a collection of fashion items. A small open case or trunk appears among the accessories. It has a pale interior and shiny trim, with fringe-like strips hanging from the upper part. The Timex name is visible inside the pale lid. Around and inside the case are colorful objects: folded scarves or fabrics in pink and orange, a red rounded purse or case, a yellow spotted accessory, and multiple wristwatches laid out like jewelry. The watches have different strap colors and styles, including white, black, and darker bands, with small metallic round or square faces. The arrangement looks like a treasure box of fashion watches spilled over bright fabric. The view lingers on the watch selection. Several watches rest on soft, swirling pink and orange cloth, their metal cases glinting under the colored lights. A white strap watch lies to the left, a dark strap watch with a round face lies toward the right, and other small watches with shiny faces are arranged across the fabric. The open Timex case remains in the background, reinforcing the brand. The pink mannequin bends over the accessories and reaches toward the display. Her pink-sleeved arms move near the chrome shelf and the scattered watches, as if choosing one. A close view then isolates one watch: a small, elegant wristwatch with a pale face and light-colored strap set against a textured deep pink background. Its case is rounded-square with a shiny metal edge, and the Timex name is faintly visible on the dial. The hands and simple hour markers are clearly shown. Another mannequin’s blue-gloved or blue-painted hands reach into the watch display. The blue figure handles a watch delicately near the open case, lifting it from the fabrics. A close view shows a different watch style: a round-faced watch with a decorative top loop and dangling ornament or chain-like piece below, presented against a rich blue background. The face is pale with simple hour markers, and the case is silver-toned, resembling a jewelry-style watch or pendant-like fashion piece. The green mannequin is shown reclining or leaning back in her flowing green outfit. She raises one arm, then brings her wrist toward herself. In close views, pale green hands fasten a watch around the wrist. The watch has a white or light dial and a dark strap. A close-up follows, showing the watch face large against green fabric: a round, silver-toned case, pale face, dark hour markers, and a dark strap, with the Timex name visible on the dial. The pink mannequin, now more animated, lifts a soft green scarf or piece of fabric near her face and chest, trying it as an accessory while standing at the shelf. She tilts her head upward, still in round sunglasses, as if admiring the look. Nearby, a striped hat or stack of striped accessories sits on the shelf above her. The blue mannequin also examines her wrist near the shelves, her blue face and hooded outfit lit by bright magenta and blue light. She adjusts or checks a watch while standing beside a small red mannequin-hand display and the same chrome shelving. The group returns to a wide boutique arrangement. The blue mannequin stands left in her draped blue garment and jewelry; the pink mannequin stands center in her pink dress, one hand on her hip and the other arm extended; the green mannequin stands right in flowing green, holding an arm outward. The boutique feels full of movement and color, with glowing bulbs and reflective surfaces all around them. The watches are shown again on the bright fabrics near the open Timex case. Several styles remain spread out: small round and square faces, light and dark straps, and shiny metal cases. The display emphasizes variety, with the watches treated like fashion accessories among scarves, purses, and jewelry. The commercial ends on a black background with another bright retro title card. In a pink decorative border, blue and white glowing text reads “TIMEX FASHION WATCHES,” with prices underneath shown as “9.95–19.95.”

A softly lit airport waiting area appears, with large bright windows on the left looking out toward a runway or open tarmac. The interior is dim by contrast, with red carpeting, lounge chairs, and baggage nearby. A middle-aged man with dark hair, wearing a dark jacket and light trousers, moves anxiously among the seats and luggage. He settles briefly near the window, then turns toward someone seated nearby. In a closer view, a young Black boy or teenager in a red top sits by the window wearing large, over-ear headphones connected to a small portable radio or listening device. The man leans in very close beside him, intent and curious, as if trying to catch what the boy is listening to. The boy keeps facing forward, absorbed in the headset, while the man peers over his shoulder. Other travelers pass through the background carrying coats and bags, reinforcing the busy terminal setting. The man then straightens and moves away through the lounge as people continue walking behind him. The scene changes to a plain deep blue background with large white serif lettering centered on screen: “United’s Friendship Service.” The same words remain briefly as the image blends into an airplane-seat armrest, where a hand reaches toward a built-in audio control panel. A small label above the controls reads “C ROW 13.” The hand plugs a dark cord into the panel, beside round and rectangular buttons and small arched selector markings. Inside the airplane cabin, the dark-haired man now sits in a passenger seat. He wears a light striped dress shirt and a red tie, with a simple airline headset or earphones placed over both ears. He adjusts the earpieces with both hands, then looks down toward the armrest controls. A close view shows his fingers turning or pressing one of the small controls on the audio panel. Rows of passengers fill the cabin behind him, seated in teal-and-light-colored seats with pale headrest covers. The man brings his hands together near his mouth for a moment, focused and tense, then relaxes as he listens. His expression changes from concentration to clear pleasure; he smiles broadly, almost grinning, while still wearing the headset. A wider view of the aircraft cabin shows several passengers seated and moving about. The man rises or turns partly in his seat, still wearing the earphones, while a female flight attendant or airline employee in a dark uniform with a red accent stands nearby. Other passengers look on casually. He glances back over the seat behind him, as if sharing or reacting to what he has just heard. Nearby, a young white woman with shoulder-length reddish-brown hair smiles warmly across the aisle or seat row. She wears a patterned blouse with large circular shapes and a tied scarf-like collar. She looks toward an elderly white woman seated beside or in front of her. The elderly woman has neatly styled white hair, black-framed glasses, pearl earrings, and a striped scarf or collar at her neck. She smiles and laughs, then looks downward with an amused expression, suggesting the good mood has spread among the passengers. The man is seen again from behind and in profile, still seated with the headset in one ear, looking over his shoulder. White serif text appears over the lower left and center of the cabin image: “The friendly skies of your land.” As the man lowers behind the seatback, the slogan remains prominent across the seat in front of him. The commercial ends on a blue screen with large white serif lettering: “United to 113 cities.”

A long line of people stretches through an almost completely white, misty space, as if they are standing on clouds. The people face away in a winding queue that disappears into the bright distance. Closest to view are various adults in ordinary clothes: a woman with a red hair bow and striped shirt, an older woman with gray hair in a patterned brown jacket, a man in a dark suit, a blonde woman, and others farther along in colorful outfits. The atmosphere is soft and overexposed, with no visible walls or floor, just white haze underfoot. At the front of the line is a white counter or podium. An elderly white-haired man in white clothing sits or stands behind it like a clerk or judge. In front of him lies a large open book or ledger with thick pages. A green banker’s lamp sits on the counter, and a white mug nearby has bold black writing that reads, “Do I Look Like I Care.” Facing him across the counter is another elderly man, thin, pale, and wrinkled, with tousled white hair, wearing a teal-blue jacket over a light green shirt. He leans forward anxiously from the line, looking up at the man in white. The man in white consults the large book while the elderly man in blue reacts with worry and confusion. The elderly man’s face shifts from puzzled to tense; he opens his mouth as if answering questions, then looks increasingly alarmed. Behind him, other people in line wait close together, including an older woman in a mint-green uniform-like dress and apron and a Black man in a dark suit. The man in white remains calm and matter-of-fact, one hand near the open book, the mug with the blunt message clearly visible beside him. As the exchange continues, the elderly man in blue becomes more distressed. His eyes squeeze shut, his mouth tightens, and he grimaces as though embarrassed or overwhelmed by what is being discussed. He turns his head slightly, clenches his face, then bends forward with a pained expression. The people behind him remain packed in the queue, watching or waiting, while the white counter and bright, cloudy background keep the scene stark and surreal. The view opens back out to the long line. It snakes far into the distance across the cloudy white floor. At the front are several distinctive figures: the Black man in a formal black suit, a person in a glossy black helmet and white outfit with a yellow belt, an older man in a dark robe, and a woman in a dark top and pale skirt. Farther back are people in colorful costumes and everyday clothing, all standing shoulder to shoulder in the same slow queue. Back at the counter, the man in white looks down at the book, then up toward the elderly man in blue. The elderly man turns his head away, as if reacting to something happening behind him. The scene cuts to the line behind him: a man in a yellow shirt and striped tie stands with his arms raised in complaint. Around him are other waiting figures, including a man in a green cap with plush brown antlers, a man in a yellow cap and green sweater holding golf clubs, and a person in a white fencing outfit with a mesh face mask. The man in yellow suddenly drops straight down through the cloudy floor; only his trouser legs and shoes are briefly visible sinking into a soft, dark-edged hole in the mist. The surrounding people react by looking down toward where he vanished. The man in the green cap with antlers bends his head, and the golfer in the yellow cap peers toward the gap while still holding his clubs. The fencer stands stiffly beside them. At the counter, the elderly man in blue turns back toward the man in white with wide eyes, looking startled by what just happened. A close view shows the man in the green cap with plush antlers now holding and eating a chocolate bar. He wears a purple sleeveless shirt and plaid shorts, and he bites into the partly unwrapped bar while standing in line. Beside him, a woman in a light purple dress with a white cap or bonnet looks downward. The candy wrapper is dark with the familiar Snickers branding colors visible, and the chocolate bar protrudes from the opened end as he eats. The commercial then presents the product against a plain white background. A wrapped Snickers bar appears centered, with the blue “SNICKERS” logo on a brown wrapper. Beneath it, bold black text reads, “Really hungry? Why wait?” A much larger Snickers wrapper slides in across the top and fills most of the screen, showing “THE BIG ONE” in large yellow-orange lettering on the left and the oversized blue “SNICKERS” logo across the bar. Finally, the scene returns to the white counter. The man in white stands behind the podium with the green banker’s lamp and the “Do I Look Like I Care” mug still on top. Two people now wait before him: a Black man in a black suit and tie, and an elderly white woman in a teal dress with a white apron. They stand side by side in the glowing white space, facing the man in white as the next people in line.

The commercial opens in a busy studio or backstage dressing-room area. Several people stand and crouch around a set filled with ladders, metal framework, equipment, and a vanity mirror lined with bright round bulbs. The lighting is dramatic, with warm bulbs and colored blue and red highlights giving the space a photo-shoot atmosphere. A young adult man with dark, wavy hair, wearing a dark jacket over a gray shirt, stands near a young adult woman. She has shoulder-length brown hair, wears a burgundy blouse tucked into light blue jeans, and has round white earrings. She faces him while holding a gray camcorder up to one eye, as if checking him through it. She lowers the camcorder and smiles at him, appearing confident and encouraging. The man is then seen more closely. He smiles, glances down, then looks toward the camera and off to the side. His dark hair is neatly styled with volume at the front, and he looks relaxed and pleased, as though he is ready for the shoot. A blurred studio background with ladders and warm lights remains behind him. The image changes to a black-and-white portrait of the same man printed on paper. In the upper left corner, the word “Simulation” appears in small white text. The portrait shows him in a dark shirt, and small white specks are visible on one shoulder, representing dandruff. A hand holding a blue pencil or marker moves across the photo and circles the speckled shoulder area in blue, drawing attention to the flakes. The woman appears again, now facing forward against the same studio background. She speaks directly to the viewer with a calm, friendly expression. Her burgundy blouse, softly styled hair, and white earrings are clearly visible. The picture then shifts to a large close view of a white Head & Shoulders bottle held in a hand. The label reads “Head & Shoulders” with “Dandruff Shampoo” underneath, and the bottle has bold curved bands of blue, red, and purple across the lower front. After the product is shown, the woman continues speaking to the viewer, still in the studio setting. She holds the white bottle partly visible at the lower left for a moment, then lowers it out of view while maintaining eye contact and a reassuring expression. A demonstration follows: the back of a man’s head fills the view, showing dark, clean-looking hair. A hand rests on top of the hair and gently parts or lifts it to reveal the scalp beneath. At the bottom of the screen, white text reads, “After 3 weeks of regular use.” In the softly blurred background, a man in dark clothing faces forward, out of focus. The hair being examined appears thick and glossy, with no visible flakes as the hand shifts through it. The commercial ends on a tabletop arrangement. Two black-and-white portrait photos of the young man lie on a dark surface; one has the blue-circled shoulder marking from the earlier “Simulation,” and the other shows him smiling cleanly. At the upper left, a purple banner with white text reads, “Great Hair Can’t Have Flakes.” Nearby are desk items including a red folder or notebook, keys, and small stationery objects. A white Head & Shoulders bottle is placed upright on the right side beside the photos, label facing outward with the same blue, red, and purple design.

Two young adult women with very similar blonde hair and matching bright blue sleeveless dresses stand side by side on an indoor balcony or upper walkway. A white railing runs across the foreground, and warm sunlight filters through blinds behind them, casting striped shadows on pale walls. Both women smile broadly and bounce in place, raising their hands as if joining in a cheerful chant or dance. Their loose hair swings as they lean over the railing and gesture outward toward the viewer. A close view presents a pale green pack of Wrigley’s Doublemint Chewing Gum held between hands with glossy red fingernails. The package is shown clearly, with the words “WRIGLEY’S DOUBLEMINT CHEWING GUM” on the front and a round “25¢” price mark. The fingers tug at one end, briefly sliding the inner gum sleeve out from the wrapper, then the pack is shown again centered and crisp against a light striped background. A bright blue sky hangs over a downtown skyline of tall glass office buildings. A green overhead road sign reads “Airport” with a white downward arrow, placing the action on an urban road leading toward the airport. The scene shifts to a small, toy-like animated taxi on a sunlit roadway. It is lime green with gray side panels, a white “TAXI” roof sign, and a black-and-white checker stripe along the roofline. A dark-haired passenger sits behind or beside him, looking forward. From the front, the little taxi drives toward the viewer on a wide, nearly empty city road with skyscrapers in the background. The black front panel clearly shows the white word “DURACELL.” The driver and passenger sit close together behind the windshield, their rounded puppet faces visible under the taxi roof sign. The car continues to look underpowered, and the smoke returns as the view cuts back to the side of the green cab. White smoke billows from the hood, drifting upward and partly covering the windshield. A closer view of the driver shows his annoyed, worried expression. He has a short gray cap pulled low, dark eyebrows, a rough stubbly chin, and the cigarette stuck at one side of his mouth. His forearm rests on the open window ledge as he looks out from the smoky cab. His mouth shape changes from open to downturned, making him look frustrated as the car fails him. The green taxi lurches along the roadside near a yellow-painted curb. It bumps onto the gravel shoulder beside the curb, the front wheels tilted and the body rocking. Smoke continues to gush from the front, and the passenger’s face is visible through the window, looking alarmed. The cab comes to a stop on the rough shoulder with the city towers still rising in the background. The image returns briefly to a cleaner, front-facing view of a yellow taxi driving smoothly down the broad road. A human hand holds a Duracell battery package, with two black-and-copper batteries visible behind clear plastic. A bright green vertical strip on the package reads “COPPER TOP TESTER,” with “GOOD” printed near the top. The white word “DURACELL” is printed vertically on the batteries. Small on-screen text at the lower left reads “Simulation,” indicating that the battery tester display is being demonstrated rather than shown as a literal real-time result. The fingers hold the package at the top and bottom while the tester strip remains centered and readable. Back on the road, the smoky green taxi sits at the roadside with the stubbly driver and dark-haired passenger looking out. A bright yellow taxi streaks past in front of them from right to left, partially blurring across the screen and momentarily blocking the view. The green cab remains stuck in a cloud of smoke, while the yellow cab looks fast and reliable by comparison. Inside the yellow cab, the driver in the yellow cap and the passenger in the brown hat glance toward each other, then forward again, both wearing small relaxed smiles. The stalled green cab is shown again from the side. The older driver leans on the window with his cigarette still in place, his face creased into a frown. The dark-haired passenger sits behind him with a worried, open-mouthed look. Wisps of smoke drift past the windows and around the cab. The yellow cab’s occupants are then shown once more from the front, sitting behind the split windshield. The driver faces the road, and the passenger smiles beside him, both appearing comfortable and untroubled. A wider view shows the contrast between the two taxis. The yellow taxi speeds away across the open roadway in the foreground, while the green taxi remains behind on the shoulder, partly hidden by a large cloud of smoke. The yellow cab exits the scene, leaving the disabled green cab alone by the curb beneath the clear blue sky and distant high-rises. A tight front view of the smoky green taxi shows the “TAXI” roof sign above the windshield. The driver’s face fills the center, frowning with the cigarette at his mouth. Behind him, a small pair of red fuzzy dice hangs from the rearview area. Smoke curls around the cab and drifts across the glass, reinforcing that the vehicle has broken down. The final roadway is an airport approach. The yellow taxi drives away from the viewer down the center of a broad road between low airport buildings. An overhead green sign reads “Departing Flights” with downward arrows. A small airplane is visible in the sky to the left. As the taxi continues forward, it visually gives way to a large floating Duracell battery on the road. The black cylindrical battery body appears with the white word “DURACELL” across its side. A copper-colored top section slides in and attaches to the black body, forming the familiar Duracell copper-top battery shape. Across the bottom of the screen, white text appears: “You Can’t Top The Copper Top.”

A silver Saturn sits in a dim, glossy showroom with cool blue and purple lighting reflected across the floor and bodywork. A slim young adult man stands on a narrow stone ledge in front of a grand public building with tall pale columns and vertical grooves. Strong sunlight casts hard shadows across the stone. He has light skin and medium-length brown hair that swings around his face. He wears a dark long-sleeved shirt, loose light-blue jeans with a torn knee, heavy brown shoes, and a red plaid shirt tied around his waist. He moves restlessly and dramatically, stepping along the ledge, throwing his arms up, and whipping his hair as if passionately arguing with someone offscreen. His face fills the view as he leans forward, scowling and speaking directly outward. His hair blows across his forehead and cheeks. He points and jabs with his hand, his mouth wide open, brows pulled tight, giving the impression of an intense rant. He turns side-on beside the columns, still gesturing with one finger, then faces forward again, glaring and speaking with exaggerated urgency. He becomes even more theatrical. With the massive columns towering behind him, he grabs both sides of his head, fingers buried in his hair, bending forward and grimacing as if overwhelmed. His hair flies loose as he shakes his head. He crouches low on the ledge, then springs up into a wide-legged stance, hands clasped over his head, before settling back into a front-facing position. He continues pacing and gesturing, sometimes looking straight ahead, sometimes down and to the side, his expression shifting between anger, alarm, and defiance. After a burst of frantic motion, he pauses and smooths his hair back with one hand, pulling it away from his face. His posture dips, and he looks downward, still tense. He then swings back into view with his hair partly covering one side of his face, speaking sharply again. A young adult woman appears behind him near a dark doorway between the columns. She has light skin, short wavy auburn hair, and wears a pale gray top under a black strappy dress or camisole, with a black choker necklace and small pendant. She stands calmly behind and slightly to his left while he continues ranting in the foreground. As she steps closer, her expression is composed and matter-of-fact. She raises a small white square packet in her hand, holding it near his shoulder level as if presenting it to him. The man notices the packet and looks down at it. The view shifts to the packet held between fingers: it is a white foil condom wrapper with the brand name “Sheik” printed in large purple script, and smaller text reading “1 Condom.” Another hand steadies or touches the packet, making the product name clearly visible. The packet is small, square, and crinkled at the edges. Back beside the columns, the woman faces outward with a calm, slightly knowing look, while the man stands to her right, now focused on the packet in his hand. She appears to have made her point. He studies the wrapper, his earlier defiance giving way to surprise. As the woman moves out of the foreground, he remains holding the Sheik packet, looking after her and then back at it. His expression changes dramatically. He brightens, eyes widening and mouth opening in sudden enthusiasm. Still clutching the packet, he gestures excitedly with his free hand and repeatedly holds the wrapper up toward the viewer. He smooths his hair back again, grinning and animated, then waves the packet as if proudly showing it off. The anger and resistance from earlier are replaced by eager approval. He continues speaking rapidly and enthusiastically, the condom packet flashing in his hand as he points it forward. His hair flips around with his movement, and he bounces in place on the ledge. In the final moment, he is again shown full-body against the tall stone columns, standing on the ledge with the red plaid shirt tied at his waist, raising both arms triumphantly above his shoulders.

The car approaches a steep loop-like path framed by plants and mechanical elements. Around him, the miniature world spreads out: floating tracks, loops, rocky islands, greenery, water, and mist. The blue car becomes one small moving point within this imaginative landscape. The blue Honda then drives down a curving road bordered by red-and-white racing stripes and enters a dramatic tunnel. The tunnel walls are lined with rows of shiny, spoon- or feather-shaped metallic pieces arranged in circular patterns, like a mechanical flower or turbine. Red and blue streaks of light trail through the dark tunnel. The car heads toward an intense white glow at the far end. Small on-screen text appears near the bottom during this sequence, including a disclaimer indicating different Civic sedan trims are being shown. As the car exits the glowing tunnel, the environment changes to a bright sky world above clouds. A blue, watery, crystalline splash sweeps over the front of the car. The white Honda sedan drives forward on a smooth elevated road surrounded by clouds, blue sky, and whimsical floating objects. From above, the road appears suspended high among clouds and treetops, with colorful ribbons, tubes, and balloon structures all around. The car speeds over scattered colored fragments on the roadway and approaches a suspended rectangular platform between the canyon walls. The platform is supported by poles and surrounded by loops, springs, and colorful mechanical decorations below. In the far background, the giant silhouette of the designer appears again, with the glowing rectangle at the back of his head, linking the scene back to his imagination. The red car reaches the end of the platform and launches into the air. It rises above the suspended roadway, centered between the canyon walls, with blue sky and clouds behind it. From inside the car, the view looks out through the windshield toward a large rainbow-colored circular track ahead. The rainbow track grows larger in front of the windshield, its bands of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and other colors forming a huge loop. A green Rolling Rock beer bottle fills the view, its white label beaded with moisture. Large blue letters read “ROLLING ROCK,” with “Extra Pale” written below and a small horse-head emblem on the side of the label. The image shifts to the back of the green glass, where a white horse-head logo and ribbon graphic appear above the words “KEEP ON ROCKIN’,” also speckled with condensation. The scene moves into a dim, warm bar with wood walls, string lights, a pool table, and small tables crowded with green beer bottles and bowls of snacks. A young adult man with light brown-blond hair, wearing a pale blue short-sleeved button-up shirt over a white T-shirt, sits at a table with male friends. She stands in front of him, raises a finger in a beckoning gesture, and leans in close over the table. The blonde woman bends nearer, her body crossing the foreground as she reaches toward him. The young man glances sideways at one of his friends, looking hesitant. They arrive near the pool table, where colorful billiard balls sit scattered on the green felt. Other young women stand and dance nearby, including a dark-haired woman in an orange tank top holding or standing near a pool cue. The blonde woman positions the young man in the open space beside the pool table. She faces him with a small, expectant smile, while he stands stiffly with his green beer bottle in hand. The blonde starts to dance in front of him, shoulders and arms moving lightly. He responds with an awkward, cautious attempt: holding the Rolling Rock bottle in one hand, he raises his other hand near his head and makes small, uncertain fist-pumping motions. Around them, other patrons continue drinking, dancing, and watching from tables. His three male friends are shown at their table, leaning forward with beers in front of them. She keeps a composed, assessing expression, occasionally lifting her hands in small dance-like motions. He begins to smile, looking more comfortable, and turns his attention off to one side. A second blonde young woman approaches from nearby, wearing a burgundy sleeveless top with light trim and her hair pulled back in a ponytail. She holds green Rolling Rock bottles, and a small tray with more bottles is visible between her and the man. The man reaches toward the bottles and takes them. The Rolling Rock labels are visible on the green glass as the bottles cluster together near chest height. The ponytailed woman smiles faintly while handing them over. The man looks down at the two bottles now in front of him, his face becoming blank and thoughtful for a moment. Across the room, his three friends grin broadly. One lifts a green bottle toward him in a silent toast while the others smile and gesture, clearly pleased with themselves. The man looks back up, now smiling with a slightly sheepish, knowing expression. The blonde woman in the black top reappears behind him, smiling too, and places a hand lightly on his shoulder. As they stand together, the Rolling Rock horse-head logo and ribbon graphic fade over them, followed by the white words “KEEP ON ROCKIN’” on the green, condensation-covered bottle glass. The commercial ends on another close view of the Rolling Rock label, with the blue “ROLLING ROCK” name and “Extra Pale” text prominent on the wet green bottle.

The commercial begins in a sleek, modern hotel lobby with polished floors, white walls, and a long reception counter glowing warmly from below. At the reception counter, the guest faces a male front-desk clerk. The clerk is a pale-skinned adult man with straight, chin-length black hair cut in a sharp bob. He wears a black suit jacket, a dark blue shirt, and a matching tie, with a small hoop earring visible in one ear. His expression is attentive and formal. The guest, a light-skinned adult man with short curly dark hair, wears an olive-tan blazer over a light blue button-up shirt. He stands slightly hunched over the counter, focused on the clerk, looking a little cautious or uncertain as he answers questions. The two men continue the check-in process. The guest leans in, looks down, and handles papers or a card on the counter. The clerk remains composed behind the desk, looking at him and occasionally looking down at the work surface. Behind them, a blonde woman in a bright pink top with a dark vest walks through the lobby, and other guests sit or pass by in the softly lit background. The guest reaches out across the counter, and the clerk extends his hand; they appear to exchange a small item, likely part of the check-in paperwork or room key. As the conversation continues, the clerk’s face fills the view several times. He keeps steady eye contact with the guest and speaks with a polished, professional demeanor. His features are very still and controlled, and the curving branches of a potted plant behind him create a decorative shape over his shoulder. The guest, seen in return, looks up at the clerk with widened eyes, then glances down and to the side as if considering what he has just been offered. He seems to agree, then looks slightly hesitant but still cooperative. The scene shifts to a hotel bedroom. A red animated M&M’s character lies on his back on a white pillow, tucked on top of the bed linens like a person placed there for turn-down service. He is round and glossy red, with large white oval eyes, black pupils, a small smiling mouth, white gloves, and white shoes. A large white lowercase “m” is printed on the top of his candy shell. His arms are bent with gloved hands resting near his sides, and his legs are raised comfortably, making him look relaxed and expectant. The red M&M remains positioned on the pillow beside the guest, visually turning the hotel’s “complimentary chocolate on your pillow” idea into a full-sized living candy character in bed.

A dusty, animated desert training camp comes into view as the back of an old gray bus drives forward between crooked fence posts and dry scrub. Through the small rear window of the bus, rounded fruit characters can be seen inside. The bus passes under a large wooden arch with bold white letters reading “FRUIT CAMP,” with lamps hanging above it and watchtowers and low camp buildings in the distance. The bus stops beside a camp area, and a line of anthropomorphic fruit characters stands outside it like recruits. They have cartoon faces, thin black arms and legs, and little boots. Among them are an orange, a pear, a banana, a green apple, a lemon, a raspberry-like red fruit, a pineapple, and other small fruit characters. In front of them stands the leader: a tall red twisted fruit-snack character with a yellow spiral stripe wrapped around his body, long black limbs, gloves, oversized black boots, and a wide-brimmed drill-sergeant-style hat. His face is stern, with heavy-lidded eyes and a big rectangular mouth full of white teeth. The red twist character strides in front of the recruits, gesturing with a long black pointer or baton. He holds up a bright yellow-and-red Kellogg’s Fruit Twistables box so the front faces outward. The package has the large blue “Fruit Twistables” logo across it and pictures of twisted fruit-snack strips near the bottom. He points at the box while addressing the fruit lineup, using exaggerated arm movements and leaning forward with a commanding expression. The recruits react nervously. A pale yellow pear with a stem on top stares wide-eyed, its mouth open in worry, while an orange beside it looks uneasy. The red twist character paces close in front of them, his long limbs and pointer crossing the foreground. The pear squeezes its eyes shut as if bracing itself, then opens them again with a startled look. The scene widens to show the whole line beside the bus. The red twist leader looms over the smaller fruit characters, holding the Fruit Twistables box and baton. A yellow lemon near the line is chewing or blowing a pink bubble. The bubble grows large in front of the lemon’s face, and the red twist leader moves past with the baton. The pink bubble bursts or collapses, leaving the lemon’s face and body splattered with pink goo. The nearby green apple, with a leaf on its stem, looks on with round eyes. The red twist leader leans in close to the lemon, his face filling the view beside the lemon’s yellow surface. He raises the baton and scowls, baring his teeth as he appears to scold the lemon. The lemon is left coated in pink patches, its eyes drooping in embarrassment or defeat. Back in the lineup, the goo-covered lemon stands beside a small red raspberry-like fruit and a tall peeled banana. The red twist leader marches past them, boots thudding through the dusty ground, while the banana watches with a nervous hand near its mouth. The wider camp setting remains visible: a gray bus behind the recruits, tan barracks, sparse desert plants, and guard towers under a bright sky. A tiny purple grape character wearing an oversized tan helmet stands between the larger fruits’ boots. The grape has a small face, thin arms and legs, and looks up anxiously as the red twist leader’s big boots move around it. The leader steps and pivots dramatically, carrying the Fruit Twistables box and baton, while the little grape remains directly in the path of the action. The red twist leader then performs an exaggerated demonstration, stretching and twisting his red-and-yellow body as if showing off the product’s “twist” theme. He leans far back, flips his hat upward, and bends his flexible body in big arcs while still holding the package. The fruit recruits watch from the side, including the tall banana, pineapple, lemon, apple, and raspberry. At one point, a huge boot sole fills the view from below, emphasizing how close the leader’s foot comes to the tiny grape. The grape reappears flattened into a shiny purple splat on a wooden crate or platform, with bits of the tan helmet and purple droplets around it. Even flattened, the grape’s cartoon face remains visible in the gooey purple puddle, giving a comic impression that it is still conscious. The red twist leader stands tall again in front of the lined-up fruit recruits, holding the baton horizontally like a command stick. The fruits stand at attention beside the bus: the orange and pear on the left, then the apple, goo-covered lemon, banana, pineapple, and small red fruits on the right. When the leader gives the final command, the fruit characters break formation and begin running in a chaotic rush. The orange and pear dash past the bus, while others scramble in different directions, kicking up dust. The commercial ends with a product display in the same camp setting. Three large Kellogg’s Fruit Twistables boxes stand upright across the dusty ground, each with the big blue “Fruit Twistables” logo and colorful fruit-snack imagery on the front. The red twist drill sergeant pops up in front of the boxes, animatedly gesturing with his gloved hands and baton. He leans toward the viewer, smiles broadly, points forward, and holds his pose between the bright packages, reinforcing the product as the final visual focus.

A large Best Buy store fills the opening view, with a deep blue exterior wall and the familiar yellow price-tag-shaped “BEST BUY” sign mounted high above glass entrance doors. In a wide aisle, the mascot dances down the center of the black-and-white floor. On the right, several adults stand near displays; one man in dark clothing raises an arm, and others watch or clap. The mascot spins from showing its plain yellow back to showing the “BEST BUY” tag front again, arms spread wide with white-gloved hands open. Its legs step wide apart in a jaunty, exaggerated dance while customers on both sides continue shopping or react with smiles. A product demonstration follows at a camcorder display. Two Black adult men, one in a dark suit and one in a green shirt, look at a small handheld video camera. A young woman employee in a blue Best Buy shirt smiles as she helps. The camcorder’s flip-out screen and a nearby small monitor show a black-and-white image of the two men grinning at close range, demonstrating that the camera is recording or playing back their faces. The employee holds or presents the camcorder while the men examine it, and the monitor beside them gives a clear view of the captured image. In the appliance department, white washing machines or dryers are lined up beneath a visible sign reading “APPLIANCES.” A male employee in a blue polo shirt and khaki pants stands with a couple: a man in a dark shirt and gray pants and a woman in a tan outfit carrying a shoulder bag. The employee opens or lifts part of a front-loading appliance door, showing the couple the machine’s interior. They stand close together, facing the product and the employee, in a typical sales consultation. At a computer counter, a woman employee in a blue shirt speaks with a man in a dark dress shirt and patterned tie. Several desktop computers and monitors sit on the counter behind them, with yellow Best Buy price cards visible on some screens. The man gestures toward one of the computers while the employee leans comfortably on the counter, both focused on the display. The view shifts to long aisles of music or media. Rows of shelves hold CDs or similar packaged items, and blue signs above sections read “ROCK & POP.” A young adult man in a gray sweater browses the shelves, holding a case and looking down as he checks the selection. The aisle stretches far into the store, with multiple identical blue category signs and other shoppers partly visible between rows. A small Best Buy tag sign is mounted at the end of one display. In another electronics area, a Black male employee in a blue Best Buy polo talks with a woman in a loose green sweater near a large white appliance or electronics unit. He gestures with one hand while she rests her hand on the counter or product surface, listening. Behind them, more employees and customers examine rows of microwaves or similar boxed white appliances, and several overhead signs glow above the department. At a black DVD display, large white letters spelling “DVD” appear above a built-in screen. A man in a light gray shirt and a blonde woman in a dark jacket stand close to the display, discussing it. The man holds a disc or small item in his hand while the woman leans in to look. The screen shows a view of the store, including a glimpse of the blue-shirted staff and the Best Buy tag mascot. As they watch, the yellow tag mascot appears in the display area, creating a playful visual connection between the product demonstration and the store mascot. A bold yellow-and-black car audio display appears next. The foreground is dominated by the glossy hood or body of a bright yellow vehicle with black racing stripes. In the background, the Best Buy tag mascot stands upright near the display while customers and employees talk along a wall of car audio components. A man leans into the open vehicle area, smiling and reaching forward as if testing or exploring the car stereo setup. The mascot remains nearby, its yellow tag front visible behind him. A young woman wearing large over-ear headphones smiles brightly while holding a CD jewel case against one side of her head. She has dark hair pulled back with a headband, red lipstick, and a casual light-colored top. She presses the headphones with both hands, tilting her head and smiling as if enjoying what she is sampling. Store shelves blur behind her, suggesting she is in the music department. Another couple examines a satellite or home entertainment display. A middle-aged man in a red plaid shirt and jeans stands beside a woman in a light sweater. They face a large white satellite dish mounted on a display. The man gestures with one hand toward the equipment while the woman looks on. A partial sign nearby reads “NEED,” though the rest is obscured. A yellow Best Buy shopping basket then passes very close in the foreground, briefly blocking most of the view with its perforated plastic sides. At the checkout or service counter, a Black female employee in a blue Best Buy shirt smiles while holding a small handheld scanner or device. A male customer in a lavender shirt stands beside a yellow Best Buy shopping basket and looks down at an item or receipt in his hands. The counter area has black-and-yellow signage and product displays behind them. The employee and customer appear relaxed and friendly as they complete the transaction. From above, a large circular yellow floor area is visible like a bright spotlight or central store feature. Several shoppers and employees move around it, and the Best Buy tag mascot stands or moves along the left edge of the circle. People cross the yellow area in different directions, some carrying items or baskets, while the mascot’s blue side and yellow tag face are visible from overhead. The scene emphasizes the busy store environment, with the mascot weaving among customers. The commercial ends back outside the store. The yellow “BEST BUY” sign is mounted high on the blue facade above the glass entrance. Large white on-screen text appears at the lower right reading “Now Open.” The glass doors and windows below reflect the store entrance area, and a small copyright notice, “© 2000 Best Buy,” appears near the lower left. The final image holds on the storefront, the big tag logo, and the “Now Open” message.

A young man in a dark suit jacket and light shirt walks up the path of a tidy suburban house with a white picket fence and gate. Back at the home, the young couple sit side by side on a blue sofa in a living room. The red-haired young woman sits on the left, watching with an expectant smile. The young woman takes the box and looks at it, then suddenly leans across the sofa to hug him. He wraps an arm around her as she embraces him tightly, the open jewelry box still in her hand. While they hug, several family members sit together on the staircase in the background, watching with delighted expressions. The storefront has a large dark entrance tower with bright white signage reading “JARED” and, beneath it, “The Galleria Of Jewelry.” Cars are parked in front, and a couple walks toward the entrance. Large white text at the lower right reads “jared.com.”

The commercial opens in a bright home kitchen and dining area. A young boy, about elementary-school age, with light brown hair and a green T-shirt, sits at a wooden dining table. Back at the tabletop contraption, a pale yellow object rolls or slides down the slanted chute beneath the hanging strips of shredded paper. The goose’s head bobs in and out of view, and its beak looks wet, with a droplet visible. The boy turns toward the table and then looks down. His attention shifts from the nest to something in his hands: a handheld Game Boy Color. Pikachu illustrations decorate the black border around the screen, and the screen displays the Pokémon logo with a dark flying Pokémon silhouette beneath it. The words “GAME BOY COLOR” are visible below the screen. Small white text along the bottom says, “Game and Game Boy sold separately.” The product packaging appears on a windowsill or ledge in a bright, flower-filled setting. The scene returns to the kitchen, where the white goose bends its long neck over the shredded-paper nest. White text “www.pokemon.com” appears along the bottom. The boy becomes blurred in the background while the goose faces forward, its round black eyes and orange beak centered, the beak slightly open as if reacting to the boy’s request.

The football action briefly gives way to a product image: golden beer pours into a tilted glass, filling it with amber liquid and a thick white foamy head. Bubbles stream upward through the beer. Then an amber Miller Lite bottle covered in condensation stands beside a frosty glass mug, with more bottles blurred behind it. The white light swells again until it fills almost everything. When the man reappears, his face is clearer and more determined. The commercial ends with the man again as a black silhouette, standing squarely before the large glowing circle. His shoulders are relaxed compared with earlier, and he faces the light directly. The chamber remains hazy and gray around him, but the sunglasses have changed his relationship to the glare: instead of recoiling or shielding himself, he stands still in front of it.

In close-up, his expression shifts through hesitation and concentration; his eyes glance down and to the side, and he leans forward into the phone. He holds the gray handset tightly against his ear with one hand, his red jacket collar and striped cuff visible. His face softens as he speaks into the receiver, looking a little embarrassed but sincere. The commercial ends on another white graphic card. The black rectangle with gold “1-800-COLLECT” appears again at the centre. A bronze or gold Oldsmobile sedan is displayed in a clean side profile, facing to the right, against a warm amber-brown studio background with a smoky, softly glowing atmosphere. The car has four doors, a long low body, dark-tinted windows, and polished wheels, with its silhouette emphasized by dramatic lighting from above and behind. The floor beneath it is dark and reflective, giving the car a showroom-like presentation. No people are visible.
