The commercial opens on a studio-like gray background with an adult woman facing forward. She has short, dark, neatly shaped hair, a warm smile, and wears a reddish cardigan over a pale yellow collared shirt. She speaks directly toward the viewer, then lifts a small green can of tuna beside her face. The front label is visible: “Chicken of the Sea” in large white lettering, with a red block reading “TUNA.” She holds the can near her cheek, presenting it with a confident, slightly playful smile. She turns the can so the metal end faces outward. The circular end of the can fills more of the view, and she points to the printed inspection seal with one finger. The lettering around the metal circle becomes readable: “Department of Commerce,” “Packed under Federal Inspection,” and “United States of America,” arranged in rings around the lid with small stars separating parts of the text. Her polished fingernail rests near the edge of the seal as she draws attention to it. The image then shifts back to the woman holding an oval serving plate. On it are pale chunks or flakes of tuna arranged with colorful garnishes, including leafy greens, a red tomato, and orange slices that look like carrots. She holds the plate at chest height, angled toward the viewer, as if offering a serving suggestion. She lowers the plate and turns slightly, revealing a dining setup beside her. A family meal scene appears around a small round table covered with a light tablecloth that has a checked or crisscross pattern and fringed edges. The same woman sits on the left. Next to her is a young girl with light brown hair, wearing a pink turtleneck or long-sleeved top, holding a sandwich with both hands. To the girl’s right sits a young boy with light brown hair swept to one side, wearing a dark shirt with wide tan stripes, also holding a sandwich. On the far right, an adult man in a tan sweater sits with his back partly toward the viewer, facing the children. The table holds plates of food, white cups and saucers, sandwiches, and small items in the center such as condiments or serving pieces. The setting is simple and staged against the same plain gray background, with wooden dining chairs visible behind them. The children eat while the woman gestures across the table, watching them with an approving smile. The girl keeps both hands around her sandwich; the boy looks down at his food and then toward the others. The man holds food in his hand and leans slightly toward the children. The family appears relaxed and cheerful, sharing the meal together. A large circular inspection seal begins to surround the family scene, as though the table is inside the printed seal shown earlier on the can. The words around the ring are large and bold: “Department of Commerce,” “Packed Under Federal Inspection,” and “United States of America.” The family remains seated at the table in the center of this ring, continuing to eat and pass food, while the seal forms a graphic border around them. The view widens into a more imaginative product display: the family at the table appears small, sitting inside the circular inspection seal on top of a giant Chicken of the Sea tuna can. The can is green, with a silver metal top. On the front, the white “Chicken of the Sea” brand name is prominent, and a red rectangle below reads “TUNA.” A small mermaid figure is visible on the side of the green label. The large federal inspection seal sits like a lid emblem, with the family meal centered inside it, visually linking the product label and inspection seal to the family eating scene. The family then reappears closer together. The woman leans in from the left with her arms around the two children. The girl in pink beams broadly, still holding part of a sandwich, while the boy in the striped shirt smiles toward her and then toward the viewer. The woman presses close to the girl’s cheek, puckering as if giving her a kiss, and all three look happy and affectionate. The commercial returns to a close view of the can’s metal end with the circular seal. A hand holds the can upright, fingers visible around the sides. The seal text is again clear: “Department of Commerce,” “Packed Under Federal Inspection,” and “United States of America.” The hand tilts and rotates the can downward so the green front label comes into view. The final product image shows the can held steadily against the plain background, with the white “Chicken of the Sea” name centered on the green label and the red “TUNA” panel below it.

A dark, futuristic room appears, with smooth curved walls and a sculptural white lounge chair on the left. A dark silhouetted figure reclines in the chair, one hand lifted. In the center, on a round white pedestal, a bright column of light glows around the Touché game board, so bright that it washes the room in white. As the glow fades, a gray-haired, older adult man appears standing on the pedestal. He wears a shiny silver, space-suit-like outfit with dark stripes down the sleeves and legs. He turns toward the seated silhouette, as if summoned to play. The scene shifts to the game itself. The Touché board sits on a white plastic base with a dark blue square grid in the middle. Along the edges are small clear game pieces shaped like short transparent cylinders on round bases. Some pieces contain colored disks, red on one side and white on the other. A hand reaches in near the lower edge of the board, where a red rectangular area and small red buttons are visible, then gestures above the grid as if explaining the rules. The silver-suited man is shown from the chest up, facing forward with wide eyes and an open mouth, looking surprised or intrigued. Then he leans over the round table, watching the board closely. He gestures with one hand, concentrating on the game. A close view of the board shows a hand lifting one of the clear pieces from the side and moving it onto a square of the blue grid. The transparent piece is set down carefully, revealing a red disk inside at the bottom. The piece sits upright on the grid, its round base resting on one square. Back at the table, the silver-suited man watches tensely. A dark, gloved or shadowed hand, belonging to the unseen opponent at the left, reaches toward the board and places or moves another clear piece. In close-up, the piece that was red is shown inside its transparent casing; suddenly the disk changes from red to white, demonstrating the game’s hidden magnetic “force” that can flip a piece to the opponent’s color. The silver-suited man reacts with surprise, bringing his hand to his mouth. The board fills the view again. The word “touché” appears in large white lowercase letters across the dark blue grid. Around it are the clear game pieces with red and white disks. A hand moves one piece from an upper square to another square on the grid. As it is pressed into place, the color inside changes to white. The board then appears with several pieces scattered across the grid: some show red disks, some show white disks, and some sit on the edge areas. The silver-suited man becomes animated and pleased. He throws his hands up and then claps or rubs his hands together over the table, smiling broadly. He looks down at the board, then toward his opponent, clearly delighted with the outcome. His posture is upright and excited, and his shiny suit catches the soft white light of the minimalist room. Near the end, the dark silhouette of the opponent rises or leans into the foreground at the edge of the table while the man continues smiling with his hands clasped. A final close view shows a clear game piece on the blue board: the disk inside is white at first, then flips to red. Over the close-up, a white rectangular “Gabriel” logo appears with black lettering and a horizontal rainbow stripe beneath it, identifying the maker.

The commercial opens outdoors in daylight beside a light-coloured house with horizontal siding and leafy branches behind it. Two Black men stand close together, smiling over a silver-and-black folding Polaroid instant camera. One man, tall and slim with a rounded afro, a moustache, and a light blue open-collar shirt, holds the camera at first and leans in as if explaining it. Beside him is a slightly shorter man with a beard and moustache, wearing a pale pink striped shirt. Both look amused and engaged, their faces close to the camera as they examine its front controls. The bearded man takes the camera into his hands while the taller man points to the front, indicating where to look and press. They bend over it shoulder to shoulder, grinning. The camera has a boxy silver face, black trim, a large circular lens area, and a raised folding viewfinder section on top. The bearded man lifts it and turns outward, preparing to photograph the people nearby. The view widens to a backyard or patio gathering. A long picnic table covered with a red-and-white checkered cloth sits in front of large windows and house siding. Around it are several adults and children, dressed in bright casual 1970s colours. Plates, baskets, and picnic items fill the table. The bearded man leans forward with the Polaroid aimed at the group, while the taller man stands behind him watching. A woman in a vest stands near the far side of the table, and children sit and turn toward the camera. The group begins to pose, smiling and looking in the photographer’s direction. Back closer on the two men, the bearded man squints through the camera and presses it to his face, concentrating. The taller man crouches just behind him, smiling broadly as he watches the picture being taken. The scene cuts to the subjects of the photograph: a smiling Black woman with swept-up hair sits between two children. On one side is a little girl with an orange bow in her hair; on the other is a boy wearing large eyeglasses, a soft blue-gray cap, and a yellow-orange top. The three lean together, smiling toward the camera. The bearded man lowers the camera slightly after taking the picture. He and the taller man look down at the camera body with anticipation. The bearded man reaches to the front of the folding camera and pulls out the developing instant print. A square white-bordered photo slides free. At first the image area is dark and indistinct. He holds it upright in front of them, and both men look at it closely. A close view of the print shows the image starting as a pale gray square, then gradually becoming clearer until the same woman and two children appear within the white Polaroid border. The two men continue holding and studying the developing picture, smiling as the image comes in. A clearer close-up of the finished Polaroid fills the view: the woman beams in the center, the little girl with the orange hair bow is on the left, and the boy in the cap and oversized glasses leans in on the right. A picnic basket with round fruit or rolls sits in front of them, and the bright outdoor background is visible behind their heads. The scene returns to the two men, both laughing and delighted. The taller man holds the finished print while the bearded man cradles the Polaroid camera. They turn toward the family at the table. The woman and children look off to the side at the photograph being shown to them. The little girl sits near the basket, the woman smiles warmly, and the boy in the cap and glasses turns his head to look, his yellow-orange shirt marked with a large dark number on the front. The bearded man then lifts the camera again, now more confident. He holds it up and gestures with one hand as if giving directions to the next subject. He raises the camera to his eye and aims. A close-up of another finished Polaroid appears: it shows the boy with the blue-gray cap and large glasses close to the camera, his face framed beside a large green balloon or ball. The white border of the instant print is visible, with a hand holding it at the bottom. Back with the two men, the bearded man works the camera again while the taller man stands close behind, smiling and looking down. The bearded man pulls another dark, freshly exposed print from the camera and lifts it up between them. They face one another with friendly excitement, the print still not developed enough to show an image. A close view shows the taller man now holding the Polaroid camera up to his eye. His hands grip the silver-and-black body, the folding top is raised, and he squints through the viewfinder as if taking his turn. He lowers the camera and looks upward, then downward, with a thoughtful expression. White on-screen text appears at the bottom: “*Suggested list price.” The commercial ends with the bearded man again holding the Polaroid camera to his eye while the taller man stands beside him, watching and gesturing with one hand. The small white “*Suggested list price.” text remains along the bottom as the two continue sharing the camera during the outdoor family gathering.

Inside a small fast-food shop or sandwich counter, a heavyset middle-aged man in a white cook’s jacket, white apron, and white paper cap holds a wall telephone to his ear. Behind him are brick walls, drink machines, and bright menu boards with small lettering; “PIZZA” and a pasta sign are partly visible. Long rolls or loaves sit in a row along the counter to his right. He looks startled and urgent, clutching the phone, pointing, and leaning forward as if giving quick instructions. Another worker in a similar white cap appears behind the counter, watching and then moving to help. The cook turns away from the phone and reaches across the counter toward an enormous, extra-long loaf. He lifts the bulky bread under one arm like a log while the other worker crouches down and pulls out supplies from below the counter. Containers, trays, and sandwich-making items come into view as both workers scramble. The mood is busy and comic because the food is oversized and the workers are rushing to gather everything. Outside, a yellow AMC Pacer is parked by the storefront. The car has a rounded, compact body, large curved windows, and a wide-looking cabin. It then appears driving along a tree-lined residential street. The yellow car moves smoothly on the road, with lawns, parked cars, and tall trees passing around it. Inside the Pacer, the sandwich maker sits in the back, dressed in the same white uniform and cap. The wide rear seat area gives him enough room to work with a very long sandwich laid across a board or tray spanning nearly the width of the car. The sandwich is open-faced at first, with rows of sliced tomatoes, meats, and other fillings arranged along the bread. A small roll of paper towels and food containers sit nearby. As the car moves, he leans over the sandwich and continues assembling it, using a pan or tray of ingredients and carefully placing items along the length of the bread while scenery slides past the side windows. The yellow Pacer turns through a quiet, leafy street. From outside, it curves around a corner and continues down the road without any visible swaying or trouble. Back inside, the cook holds a small ingredient in one hand and a long thin pick or skewer in the other. A closer look shows his hands delicately handling a small green garnish, likely an olive or pickle piece, as he threads or prepares it for the sandwich. The oversized sandwich remains directly below his hands. In the front seat, another middle-aged man in a white paper cap drives. He has glasses and a moustache, with the steering wheel in front of him and trees passing outside. He glances back while tasting something from his fingers, then raises his hand in an “OK” gesture, signaling approval. The Pacer arrives at a large white mansion with tall columns, balconies, and a sweeping driveway. A formally dressed man in a black tuxedo and bow tie stands outside near the front steps, waiting. The yellow Pacer pulls up along the curb in front of the house and stops. The tuxedoed man remains poised in front of the grand entrance. Finally, the sandwich maker stands outdoors in front of the yellow AMC Pacer, holding the finished giant sandwich horizontally across his chest on a long tray. The sandwich is almost as wide as the car behind him. The cook faces forward in his white uniform and cap, while another person is partly visible behind him near the car. Large white on-screen text appears over the lower part of the image: “AMC Pacer,” with the AMC red-white-blue logo between the words. Beneath it, smaller text reads, “The first wide small car.” In the final image, the lower text changes to “Backed by the AMC Buyer Protection Plan,” while the cook continues holding the enormous sandwich in front of the parked yellow Pacer.

A young adult woman with curly red hair stands against a dark studio background with a warm reddish glow behind her. She wears a light button-up shirt with a narrow red tie and dark, shiny overall-style straps over the front. Facing forward, she smiles slightly and speaks as if introducing her choice. She then lifts an old-fashioned black telephone into view, holding it with both hands. The phone has an antique look: a dark upright stand, a separate earpiece or receiver, and a round dial area on a base. She turns her head toward it admiringly, then back toward the viewer, presenting it as if it reflects her personal taste. The scene changes to an elderly woman with short, light-colored hair, also in a dark, warmly lit setting. She laughs broadly while holding a fluffy cat close to her chest. Beside her is a bright novelty telephone shaped around a Mickey Mouse figure: Mickey stands on a red base with yellow shoes, with a yellow handset set vertically along one side. The cat looks forward while the woman cuddles it, and the playful phone sits prominently in front of them as one of her carefully chosen “friends.” Small white copyright text is visible near the bottom of the Mickey phone base. A tabletop display follows, crowded with many telephones of different eras, colors, and shapes. The arrangement is dense and theatrical, lit from above against a dark background. At first, antique models dominate: wooden and brass-looking phones with rotary dials, upright candlestick styles, and polished black or dark brown handsets. Mixed among them are more modern push-button desk phones in cream, white, tan, and brown. A glossy red phone, a cream rotary phone, and the Mickey Mouse novelty phone are also visible among the collection. The phones overlap across the table, suggesting a wide variety of personal styles, from decorative antiques to sleek contemporary designs. As the display continues, the view settles more and more on a plain white push-button desk telephone near the center. It has a rectangular sloped base with a grid of square buttons and a white handset resting across the top. Around it are other phones: a tan phone to the right with its handset in place, a red phone behind it, a cream rotary phone farther back, and darker models to the left. The white push-button phone becomes the visual focus, standing out as simpler and more standard than the more decorative phones surrounding it. A hand reaches in at the top of the white phone and lifts away its outer shell or casing. The smooth white exterior rises off, revealing that beneath the stylish surface is the actual working telephone mechanism: a compact keypad assembly with black square buttons, metal supports, exposed wiring, and internal components sitting in the base. The contrast is clear visually—the attractive outer form is only the cover, while the essential functioning parts underneath are what make it a real telephone. Finally, a bald adult man in a white suit jacket and white turtleneck appears against the same dark background with a warm amber halo behind him. He smiles gently and holds up a distinctive white telephone shaped like a smooth circular ring or rounded sculptural form. A white cord hangs down from one side. He presents it at chest height with both hands, centered in front of him, as if displaying his own obvious choice. The commercial ends with the emphasis on choosing a genuine Bell phone in a style that suits the individual.

A clean, softly lit bathroom appears, with pale walls and a bright yellow floor. On the left are bathroom furnishings, including a white chair and sink area, while the center has shelves holding folded towels and small objects. A green bath mat lies on the floor near a glass shower door. On the right edge, part of a white toilet is visible. The view gradually moves closer to the toilet tank, passing a tall plant-like stand or decorative object near the shower. The white toilet tank fills more of the scene against a plain light wall. As it comes closer, the image changes into a miniature demonstration setting: a tiny man in a nautical captain’s outfit stands on top of a large blue Ty-D-Bol package. He is a middle-aged, light-skinned man wearing a white captain’s cap with a dark brim and emblem, a dark blazer, white turtleneck, and white trousers. Beside him is a small white model toilet bowl, and above him are two large white tubes or chutes suspended from above. A close view of the captain shows him speaking directly outward, then glancing upward and raising one finger as if making a point. Back in the miniature set, the two overhead chutes are clearly labeled in bold black letters: “LEMON” on the left and “BORAX” on the right. The captain stands between them on the blue product package, gesturing up toward the tubes. Yellow lemon-like pieces pour from the left chute, while a white stream pours from the right chute, both directed downward toward the product area below him. The scene changes to a simplified close-up of blue liquid or cleaner entering a pale surface. A dark blue, spreading cloud forms beneath the opening, and bold white letters appear over it, assembling the phrase “LEMON FRESH BORAX.” The letters are large and outlined, sitting on top of the blue cloud as it expands. Next, the inside of a toilet bowl is shown from above, framed by a dark rim. Pale blue water swirls around the bowl in curved streaks. Large white text appears inside the bowl reading “tougher on stains.” The blue color deepens toward the drain area, suggesting cleaner spreading through the water. The words break apart into clusters of small white dots, which then gather and move in curved paths along the swirling blue water. Another bold white phrase appears: “tougher on odors.” Again, small white bubble-like dots arc through the bowl as the blue cleaner continues to spread and swirl. The miniature captain reappears standing beside a blue Ty-D-Bol package and the small white model toilet bowl. The package has a bright yellow label with the Ty-D-Bol name, and the small toilet bowl is connected to tubing or a curved fixture, reinforcing the product-in-use demonstration. The captain stands upright near the product, one hand raised as if continuing to explain. The commercial ends with two Ty-D-Bol bottles displayed side by side on a white surface, likely a toilet tank lid. Both bottles are blue with yellow caps and yellow labels. White on-screen text above the smaller bottle on the left reads, “Ty-D-bol Regular Lemon Fresh Blue with BORAX.” White text above the larger, wider bottle on the right reads, “New Ty-D-bol Economy Size with BORAX.”

The commercial begins with an extremely close view of a fair-skinned adult man’s face against a black background. He has short light-blond hair, light-colored eyes, and a serious, direct expression as he looks straight ahead and speaks. The image itself looks like it is being viewed on an old television or video monitor: faint horizontal lines, color bands, and momentary distortions pass across his face. Only part of his clothing is visible at first, but he appears to be wearing a dark sweater over a light patterned collared shirt. The close view continues as he talks, his mouth moving steadily and his eyes occasionally shifting slightly. The lighting emphasizes the front of his face while the background remains dark, giving him a controlled, studio-like presence. His expression stays calm and matter-of-fact, as if he is explaining something directly to the viewer. The view widens to reveal him standing in a dim domestic-looking room. He is on the left, wearing a navy or dark sweater over a checked shirt. To his right, on a table, sits a compact television set with a pale screen, and beside or in front of it is a large rectangular Zenith video cassette recorder. The recorder has a dark body with a lighter metallic top panel, a top-loading cassette area, a row of rectangular white push buttons along the front edge, and control knobs on the right front side. The room behind him is softly lit, with dark walls and framed pictures faintly visible, creating the feel of a living room or den. He turns toward the recorder and places his hand on it, demonstrating its use. He reaches over the top panel near the cassette opening, then the view changes to a closer look at the machine. A hand moves across the top controls and presses one of the white rectangular buttons in the row. The recorder’s top surface shows several compartments and switches, including the open cassette slot area and the clean, mechanical layout of the controls. The recorder is then shown with the television behind it displaying a football game: players in red and white uniforms move across a green field. The man’s hand continues to operate the controls on the recorder, suggesting recording or playback. At the bottom of the image, small white text appears; it includes “ACTUAL CLOSED-CIRCUIT TV PICTURE” and “TWO HOUR RECORDING TIME.” The machine remains prominent in the foreground while the TV picture demonstrates what it can show or record. A closer view focuses on the right front controls of the recorder. The man’s hand turns a large round knob set into a dark control panel bordered by a thin light outline. Above it, the top panel of the recorder shows more switches and a long rectangular display or label area. His fingers rotate the knob, then move away, leaving the control set. The man reappears in a closer side view, turning his head back toward the viewer. His face is now shown from the shoulders up, with the dark room blurred behind him. He looks directly ahead again, speaking with a composed expression. The checked collar of his shirt is clearly visible above the dark sweater. He continues facing forward, explaining while remaining still and centered, with only small movements of his mouth and head. Near the end, a translucent product graphic begins to overlay his face. The Zenith brand name appears in bold white lettering above a slogan. As the overlay becomes clearer, the text reads: “ZENITH” and beneath it, “The quality goes in before the name goes on.” The man’s face fades into the background while the product becomes more prominent. The final image presents the Zenith video cassette recorder alone against a dark, softly lit background. The recorder sits centered, its metallic top controls, row of white buttons, cassette opening, and right-side knobs clearly displayed. Above it, the white Zenith logo and slogan remain on screen: “The quality goes in before the name goes on.”

A silver-haired older woman identified by on-screen text as “Martha Raye denture wearer” walks onto a studio set. She has a bright, broad smile and wears a loose lavender tunic over white pants, with a white necklace or trim at the neckline. Around her are visible television-production objects: a large blue studio camera on a pedestal stands to her right, overhead lights hang above, and a wooden director’s chair to her left has her name printed on the back. She moves toward the viewer, smiling and gesturing with one hand as if addressing the audience directly. She pauses near the large camera, still smiling, then gestures toward it with a playful, confident expression. The setting then shifts to a dressing-room vanity area. She stands beside a wide mirror bordered with round glowing bulbs. Her reflection appears in the mirror on the left, while the real figure stands on the right. The counter is cluttered with dressing-room items, including boxes, small containers, and a vase of red flowers. She turns toward the viewer, smiles, and picks up a small teal-green box from the vanity. Holding the box beside her face, she presents it clearly. A close view shows the package: a teal box with large yellow lettering reading “Polident,” smaller text reading “Extra Strength” and “Denture Cleanser,” and a white circular tablet graphic surrounded by bubbles. Her fingers grip the sides of the box, and the lavender of her outfit is blurred behind it. She then appears again in the dressing room, smiling while holding the Polident box up near her cheek. The commercial moves into a product demonstration. A hand holds a set of dentures against a dark background. The teeth and gum line are visibly marked with heavy brownish stains, especially along and between the teeth. The stained dentures are lowered into a clear cylindrical glass. White lettering on the glass reads “Extra Strength Polident.” The dentures sit at the bottom in liquid. A hand drops a tablet into the glass, and white-blue foam begins to bloom and swirl around the dentures. The liquid becomes cloudy and effervescent, filling much of the glass with cleaning action. White on-screen text appears near the bottom: “15 minutes later.” A hand reaches into the glass and lifts out the dentures, now appearing bright white. In a close view, two hands hold the cleaned denture sections apart, showing smooth white surfaces and clean spaces between the teeth, with the earlier brown staining no longer visible. The “15 minutes later” text remains at the bottom during this reveal. The scene returns to the dressing room. Martha Raye stands in front of the lit vanity mirror, smiling broadly in her lavender outfit, with the flowers and dressing-table objects still behind her. She speaks toward the viewer, then raises the teal Polident box beside her face again. White on-screen text appears across the lower part of the image: “Polident green gets tough stains clean.” She holds the product steady near her cheek, alternating between a knowing look and a big smile, keeping the package label visible as the commercial ends.

A fair-haired toddler with pale skin is shown bare-chested against a large wall chart made of square grid lines. A red zigzag line behind him slopes downward and ends in a downward arrow, like a falling stock-market graph. He looks upward with a solemn, slightly worried expression, holding a narrow strip of paper in both hands. As he turns his head and looks down, his face stays serious and puzzled. The setting widens into a small staged office or stockbroker’s space. The toddler is wearing a white disposable diaper and stands beside a wooden pedestal topped with a shiny gold ticker-style machine under a clear dome. A long paper tape trails from the machine down toward him. Behind him, the red falling graph remains on the wall, and to one side are shelves with books and office objects. Loose paper and colourful books or folders lie scattered on the floor. The toddler pulls at the ticker tape, then raises one hand to the top of his head as if confused or distressed. He lowers his hand and touches the tape or the machine again. In a closer view, he looks down, then brings his fingers to his mouth and chin, appearing thoughtful and concerned. A box of Kleenex Huggies disposable diapers appears on a plain light background. The box is white with red side panels and large red “Huggies” lettering, with “Kleenex” above it. On the front is a picture of a crawling baby wearing a diaper. Readable wording on the box includes “disposable diapers” and “with elastic … to help stop leaking!” A white diaper is then displayed in front of the package, opened out to show its thick, soft-looking padding and gathered elastic edges. The diaper fills the foreground while the Huggies box remains behind it. The product demonstration moves closer. A hand presses a thumb into the white diaper material, showing the padding compressing under pressure. Then the diaper is shown on a baby’s body at the leg opening. An adult hand slides two fingers along the edge of the diaper where it meets the baby’s upper thigh, then gently lifts the gathered elastic away from the skin and lets it sit back snugly, emphasizing the soft elastic fit around the leg. The toddler returns in the office scene, now with a more upbeat setting. The wall chart behind him has changed to a blue zigzag line climbing upward and ending in an arrow pointing up. Several Huggies boxes are stacked near the wall. The toddler, still in a white diaper, walks barefoot across the floor through piles of pale ticker tape. He approaches the wooden pedestal with the gold ticker machine and reaches for the long strip of tape feeding from it. A grey office keypad or calculator sits off to the side. He pulls and handles the tape while standing in front of the rising blue chart and the stacked diaper boxes. Large red product lettering fills the screen: “Kleenex Huggies,” with “disposable diapers” below it. The logo is bold and slanted, matching the red branding on the package. Back in the office, the toddler smiles broadly and laughs while moving among the scattered ticker tape. He dips down out of sight, leaving a Huggies box visible behind him in front of the blue rising graph. He pops back up with long strips of ticker tape draped over his head, shoulders, arms, and chest like streamers. The pale paper hangs over his hair and face as he grins, lifts his arms, and plays with the strips, ending the scene happy and wrapped in the celebratory paper.

A square glass perfume bottle appears against a warm amber background. It has rounded shoulders, golden liquid inside, a black rectangular cap, and a small black label on the front. Large black letters behind it spell “ARPEGE,” with “LANVIN PARIS” beneath. The bottle shifts across the lettering so that parts of the word are alternately covered and revealed. Its glass catches dark reflections along the sides, while the overall colour palette stays soft gold and sepia. The background gradually changes from the plain product graphic into a Paris view at sunset. The bottle remains large in the foreground, now set before a river and darkened city silhouette. The Eiffel Tower stands in the distance on the right, and a bridge crosses the water behind the bottle. The perfume’s amber contents glow in the fading light, echoing the colour of the sky. A pair of elegant, light-skinned hands with long pale nails and a ring opens a small black presentation box on a polished wooden surface. The word “ARPEGE” is visible on the lid. As the lid lifts, a square perfume bottle is revealed nestled inside, framed by a thin pale border. The bottle’s dark cap and amber liquid are visible as the box opens fully. A dark, spotlighted tabletop scene opens on two young adult players facing each other across a small round table. After identifying her word, the woman looks up toward the man with a pleased, open-mouthed smile. He resumes speaking to the viewer, holding the Flavettes bottle up near his shoulder so the label faces forward. The bottle is small enough to fit easily between his fingers. He alternates between presenting it and gesturing with his free hand. His posture remains composed and professional, and his eyes return often to the viewer. At moments he holds the bottle closer to his face, as if making sure the label is clearly seen, and at other moments he lowers it briefly while continuing to explain. Later, he brings the bottle back into a prominent position, using both hands briefly to frame or steady it. His gestures become more emphatic: he pinches his fingers together as if indicating a small tablet, then opens his hand toward the viewer. He holds the bottle beside his tie, label forward, and nods slightly while speaking. The study background stays the same, with the dark rows of books behind him and the lamp and fireplace at the sides. Near the end, the product becomes the main visual again. A larger image of the Flavettes label rises in front of the man, filling much of the center of the screen. The words “Flavettes” and “helps curb SMOKING and APPETITE” are clearly visible. This transitions to a product-only display: the small bottle stands centered against a plain dark background, its light cap and white label sharply contrasting with the darker surroundings. A decorative emblem reading “Norwich Products” appears superimposed over the bottle, with additional words below that appear to say “tested and tested,” though the overlap makes some of the lettering difficult to read. The emblem sits across the middle of the bottle like a seal or guarantee mark. The image then returns to the man in the study, with the Norwich emblem fading away in front of him. For the final moments, he holds the Flavettes bottle in one hand and a cigarette in the other. The cigarette is slender and light-colored, held upright between his fingers, while the bottle is held closer to his chest with the label facing forward. He gestures between the cigarette and the bottle, then points directly to the Flavettes label, visually contrasting the two objects. He finishes looking straight ahead, calm and confident, with the product still clearly displayed in his hand.

The commercial is in black and white. It opens outdoors on a sunny lawn, where several young children sit around a small party table covered with a checkered tablecloth. A smiling middle-aged woman with short, styled dark hair stands beside a top-loading washing machine. She wears a sleeveless light-colored house dress or blouse-and-skirt outfit with a fitted waist. She looks toward the viewer as she works, presenting the laundry as something she is about to handle. She turns to her left and reaches for a large box of Oxydol detergent. She brings it forward and holds it against her torso so the front label faces outward. The package has a bold circular design with the large word “Oxydol” across the front. She smiles while displaying it, then sets the box near the washer and reaches for a small cup. Holding the Oxydol box in one hand and the cup in the other, she pours detergent from the box into the cup. The garments are all light and crisp-looking: a little dress with a belt on the left, a short-sleeved shirt in the center, and long pants or overalls on the right. She continues holding the shirt open, then lowers it onto the counter in front of her, smoothing and folding the fabric while the Oxydol box remains upright at her left. She gestures to the box with one hand and to the clean garments with the other, then reaches to the counter and picks up the short-sleeved shirt again. Holding it by the shoulders, she presents it squarely toward the viewer. The shirt has a small collar and short sleeves, and it appears smooth and bright. The commercial opens in a dim, glossy nightclub-like space lit with red, blue, green, and amber lights. The gameplay footage then shows Lara in a sunlit architectural setting resembling an old European city, with cream-colored walls, balconies, arched windows, and a brick wall rising to the right. On-screen graphics appear: a “T” rating icon in the upper left, a PlayStation logo in the lower left, a colored health bar near the upper right, and the “TOMB RAIDER II” logo in orange and red at the lower right. Wooden boxes line the right side, and the water churns behind the boat as it passes through the canal. Next, Lara swims underwater in a blue-green ruin. Stone columns and walls rise around her, and her body is horizontal as she moves through the submerged space. A blue bar appears near the top right, suggesting an underwater status meter, while the Tomb Raider II branding remains at the lower right. The scene has a murky, ancient-temple look, with Lara moving between columns in the dim water. The gameplay moves indoors to a yellow-lit stone corridor with a checkered floor and carved walls. Lara runs forward into a dark opening at the far end, her small figure centered in the passage. The health bar is still visible near the top right, the rating icon remains at top left, the PlayStation logo at bottom left, and the Tomb Raider II logo at bottom right. The corridor grows darker as she advances, with columns and patterned stone panels sliding past on either side. The commercial ends back in the nightclub setting with the same woman in the black corset outfit and feather boa. She is shown closer now from about the waist up, standing with one hand at her hip and the other hand raised near her mouth or chin in a teasing pose. The club’s curved neon lines and blue light glow behind her. At the lower left, the white “EIDOS” logo appears, identifying the publisher, while the Tomb Raider II branding is partially visible at the lower right.

A young woman with light skin and long, wavy light brown to blonde hair sits cross-legged on a patterned rug. She wears light blue jeans, a loose cream ribbed sweater with a high neck, and purple canvas sneakers with white rubber toes and white laces. At first, only her lower body and hands are prominent as she bends over one sneaker, tying the laces. A bicycle wheel is visible on the left side of the room, and a white bed or sofa with soft bedding is on the right. Pale curtains and light-colored walls give the room an airy, casual feel. As she finishes with her shoe, she lifts her head and settles into a relaxed seated position, one knee raised close to her chest. She looks directly toward the viewer as if speaking conversationally. Her expression is open and friendly; she smiles lightly, then speaks with small facial changes, glancing upward briefly before returning her gaze forward. The room remains softly out of focus behind her, with the bicycle, a low piece of furniture, and the white bed or sofa framing her. She continues talking from the same seated position, now more centered and comfortable. Her posture is informal, arms resting around her knees. She smiles more broadly at moments, then leans and gestures with both hands as if explaining a point. Her sleeves are long and loose, covering part of her hands as she moves. She shifts her legs slightly, swings one arm across her body, and folds her arms loosely in front of her, keeping eye contact with the viewer. Her manner appears confident and easygoing. A product demonstration appears: a close-up of a white sanitary pad set against a dark background with pink-toned material around it. The pad’s surface has a bright white center and raised, curved side areas that visually suggest channels or barriers along the edges. At the bottom, small white all-capital text reads, “VS. LEADING REGULAR SIZED THICK NON-WINGED MAXIS.” The pad is shown in a stylized way, with the center glowing softly and the side contours clearly emphasized. The young woman reappears briefly, smiling and leaning forward with her arms folded, still in the same bright room. Then the product demonstration returns. The pad’s curved channels are again visible, and the view transitions into a side-by-side comparison. On the left is a white pad labeled “Leading Regular Maxi”; on the right is a white pad labeled “Always with Channels.” Each side has a small metal dropper positioned above the pad surface. Blue liquid begins to flow from both droppers. On the left, the liquid forms a wavy blue streak that runs down the pad surface toward the lower edge. On the right, the blue liquid travels in a narrower, more controlled line along the textured surface near the channel area. As the comparison continues, the left-side liquid looks heavier and more spread out, with a droplet collecting near the bottom edge, while the right-side liquid appears guided inward along the channel shape rather than spilling broadly across the side. The scene returns to a close view of the young woman’s face. Her blue eyes and light makeup are visible, and her long hair falls around her shoulders. She continues speaking directly to the viewer, smiling gently. Behind her, the white bedding and softly lit curtains remain visible, with small indistinct objects on furniture in the background. She tilts her head slightly as she talks, her expression shifting between thoughtful and pleased. A wider view shows her again seated cross-legged on the rug in the same room. She lifts one hand near her face, then rests it at her neck and brushes her hair back, still addressing the viewer. The white all-capital disclaimer text reappears along the bottom: “VS. LEADING REGULAR SIZED THICK NON-WINGED MAXIS.” In closer views, she leans slightly to one side and smiles warmly, her hair swept over one shoulder. The disclaimer stays at the bottom while she continues speaking, ending with a bright, direct smile. The final image is a teal product package or product card filling the screen. A green banner at the upper left says “NEW.” Near the top is the Always circular logo, with a pink and dark teal swirl inside. Large white text reads “always with CHANNELS,” and a dark teal band across the lower portion reads “MAXI with WINGS.” The packaging uses clean, bold white lettering against the turquoise background, presenting the product name clearly.

Two young adult women with very similar blonde hair and matching bright blue sleeveless dresses stand side by side on an indoor balcony or upper walkway. A white railing runs across the foreground, and warm sunlight filters through blinds behind them, casting striped shadows on pale walls. Both women smile broadly and bounce in place, raising their hands as if joining in a cheerful chant or dance. Their loose hair swings as they lean over the railing and gesture outward toward the viewer. A close view presents a pale green pack of Wrigley’s Doublemint Chewing Gum held between hands with glossy red fingernails. The package is shown clearly, with the words “WRIGLEY’S DOUBLEMINT CHEWING GUM” on the front and a round “25¢” price mark. The fingers tug at one end, briefly sliding the inner gum sleeve out from the wrapper, then the pack is shown again centered and crisp against a light striped background. The scene moves to a sunlit bedroom or sitting room with tall windows and white blinds. Two young women, again similar in appearance and energy, jump and bounce together on a bed. One wears a purple sleeveless top with white pants; the other wears a straw hat, a colorful patterned shirt, and bright yellow shorts. Cushions and bedding fill the foreground, and the room feels airy and domestic. They laugh, sit, spring up again, and kick their legs playfully while facing each other and the room. Another close product view shows the same green Doublemint pack against a warm yellow background. Hands hold the wrapper at both ends and slide the inner gum sleeve in and out, emphasizing the pack and its front label. The “25¢” circle remains visible near the right side of the package. A blue, water-textured background appears with large white capital letters. First the word “NO” is centered near the top, then “SINGLE” appears below it, forming the phrase “NO SINGLE.” The letters are bold, white, and slightly shadowed against the rippling blue backdrop. A close-up shows the young woman in the straw hat from the bedroom scene. She has long blonde hair, dangling earrings, and a colorful shirt collar visible beneath the brim. She lifts a small white piece of gum to her mouth with her fingers, places it in, and smiles upward with a pleased, bright expression. In an outdoor plaza with white arches and a fountain behind them, a young man and a young woman stand together looking at a large unfolded map. The man wears a blue shirt with light pants and carries a yellow shoulder bag. The woman has long red hair, wears a yellow shirt with a dark vest and jeans, and carries a patterned shoulder bag. Wind whips the map and her hair. She points decisively off to the right as if spotting a direction, while he struggles with the flapping map. The map billows up over his face; he lifts it above his head, and the two of them react animatedly, turning toward each other and then toward the fountain and arches. A tranquil ocean scene follows. A young woman in a bright red swimsuit rises from calm blue water. She holds a large pale shell or shell-shaped object above her head and pours water over herself; the water cascades down her face and shoulders in a sparkling sheet. As the water falls away, she smiles broadly. She lowers the shell, splashes, and laughs, holding it up beside her in the open sea under a soft blue sky. At a sunny poolside overlooking the ocean, several people relax in swimsuits. A young woman in a neon green bikini reclines at the edge of the pool wearing sunglasses; nearby, others sit and talk on the pool ledge and lounge chairs. In the foreground, a middle-aged, shirtless man with curly dark hair and a rounded belly stands in blue swim trunks, glancing toward the woman in green. He pulls himself upright and appears to suck in his stomach, then smiles and walks out of the foreground, leaving the lounging group visible behind him. The blue water-textured graphic returns with the same bold white words: “NO” and then “NO SINGLE,” again centered on the screen. At sunset by the ocean, a couple stands close together against a warm orange and purple sky. The woman, a blonde adult in a light beige top, leans back in the arms of a man wearing a dark red shirt. They smile at each other intimately. She lifts a small piece of gum to her mouth while he watches, then she laughs and reaches her arm up around him. The soft sunset colors frame them as they hold each other. The same couple appears among a row of white lounge chairs arranged diagonally across the foreground. They tumble playfully onto one of the chairs, laughing and leaning into each other. The chairs create repeating white slats across the scene, with the sunset glow low on the horizon behind them. On a calm lake bordered by green reeds and trees, two adult women with short blonde hair paddle a red canoe. Both wear red plaid shirts and smile widely. One sits in front holding a wooden paddle across the canoe, while the second woman sits behind her, also paddling. They lean slightly with the motion of the boat and laugh together as the canoe glides forward. The final scene is on a city street beside a red double-decker bus. At the open rear doorway, a young woman in a yellow jacket, plaid skirt, dark tights, and a small crossbody bag steps up toward a man standing inside the bus entrance. He wears a light sweater and tan pants and holds the vertical pole by the doorway. They smile and interact warmly as she climbs aboard. On the red side panel of the bus, a large white advertisement displays a green pack of Wrigley’s Doublemint gum with the round “25¢” mark. Beneath the package, large black text reads, “There’s no single gum like it.” As the bus scene continues, the couple remains at the doorway on the left while the gum poster fills more of the right side, ending with the package and slogan clearly visible.

The commercial opens in stark black and white with two young faces filling the screen side by side. Both appear anxious and wide-eyed, with only parts of their faces visible at the edges. Red question marks appear over their foreheads and cheeks, suggesting uncertainty about where a pimple might appear. A young man’s face then fills the image; he has dark, tousled hair and a small pimple centered high on his forehead. A round magnifying glass swings down over the pimple, and inside the glass appears a tiny bald, bespectacled man’s head, grinning broadly. Handwritten text beside him reads “Hi,” as if the pimple or acne bacteria is cheerfully announcing itself. Tiny versions of the same bald, glasses-wearing head appear on a woman’s cheek and forehead, then on the young man’s face. He looks around with exaggerated alarm as more of the little heads pop up across his forehead, cheeks, nose, and chin. The image then widens to show the young woman and young man together beneath large handwritten words reading “Acne Bacteria,” with a green curved underline. Small text in the lower left reads “SIMULATED BLACKLIGHT DEMO.” The lighting shifts to a blue blacklight effect, and both faces are covered with glowing green dots, making the bacteria appear spread across their skin. A sudden bright graphic fills the screen with huge hot-pink letters spelling “OXY” against a white background. The two young people appear small beneath the giant logo, moving playfully in the open white studio space. Turquoise handwritten-style lettering reading “sensitive” overlays the pink OXY logo, followed by the word “New” below it and a small turquoise diamond-shaped product mark. The style remains high-contrast and graphic, mixing black-and-white people with bright pink, blue, and green product colors. The young man appears again on the left, smiling and speaking expressively, with handwritten text to his right reading “VIRTUALLY No Drying.” The words curve loosely across the white background. He pulls exaggerated faces and leans partly out of view, as if reacting comically to the claim. A young woman then appears beside the words “VIRTUALLY No Irritation.” She has messy, teased hair with dangling earrings and a concerned, pouty expression. Bright pink blotches are painted over her forehead and cheeks as visual symbols of irritation, while small text at the bottom says “SEE PACKAGE FOR DETAILS.” The two young people stand together under a large handwritten “GUARANTEED,” arched across the top with a pale blue underline. The young man moves toward the young woman and wraps his arms around her in an enthusiastic hug, lifting one leg behind him in a playful pose. This dissolves into another blacklight-style image of the young man’s face, now tinted blue with glowing green spots. Large hands enter from both sides, with index fingers extended like pointers, aiming at the spots on his cheeks and forehead. As the hands sweep across his face, the green marks fade. He ends facing forward with a broad, slightly goofy smile, while handwritten names of days of the week appear around him, including “Sun,” “Thur,” “Fri,” and “Tue,” suggesting daily use. A row of bald, glasses-wearing heads, representing the acne bacteria, peek over a curved gray surface like little figures hiding behind a wall. They grin and look around. Behind them, a turquoise Oxy Sensitive package rises into view. As it grows larger, handwritten words such as “HELP” and “NO” appear around the scene. The product package dominates the center: it is turquoise with a black diamond panel reading “sensitive,” large pink “OXY” lettering, blue “sensitive” text, and a black strip with yellow “VANISHING” visible near the bottom. The bald heads remain scattered around the lower edge, reacting as the package looms above them. The young woman returns under the blue blacklight effect, with glowing green spots on her face and the on-screen instruction “USE ONLY AS DIRECTED” in the upper left. She rubs or wipes her cheek and around her mouth with her hand. As her hand moves away, her face looks clearer and she smiles. The turquoise product package slides in from the right, partly covering her face, then fills much of the screen before moving aside to reveal the young man again. He faces forward in black and white, one eye squeezed shut in a wink and his mouth open mid-expression. Blue radiating lines appear on both sides of his head, adding a graphic emphasis to his reaction. Two floating bald heads appear on a plain white background: one wears regular black glasses and smiles, while the other wears dark sunglasses and has a small mustache. Pink-red heart shapes pop around them, implying the bacteria are multiplying or “breeding.” A thick red diagonal bar sweeps across them, forming a prohibition symbol. The completed red circle-and-slash sign surrounds the two heads, with handwritten white text around it reading “Oxycute ’em in Advance.” The heads look trapped inside the “no” symbol. A small turquoise Oxy Sensitive package appears beneath curved handwritten text reading “Product Shot,” with “Invisible Gel” written below it. The package tilts slightly on the white background, again showing the turquoise color, black diamond “sensitive” panel, pink OXY logo, and the vanishing/invisible gel branding. Finally, a circular cutout opens in a white surface. The young man appears inside the circle, then the young woman joins him, smiling and putting an arm around his shoulders. Large turquoise, three-dimensional-looking text arcs above them reading “Oxycute ’em.” At the bottom, the “SB SmithKline Beecham” logo appears, closing the commercial with the couple framed together and the product slogan hovering overhead.

A stark, gray, futuristic chamber appears, with smooth metal or concrete walls, circular porthole-like openings, and a cone-shaped fixture jutting from one wall. In the middle of the room, a lone adult man stands near a short cylindrical pedestal. He is light-skinned, with long brown hair tied back, light stubble, and a tense, guarded expression. He wears a loose blue-gray overshirt over a dark T-shirt, giving him a rough, non-uniform look against the rigid, institutional surroundings. His hands are shown close up. A metal band or cuff is visible around one wrist, and his fingers work at a dark strap or restraint near his body. He grips and pulls at a small metal piece as if loosening or freeing himself. The imagery then shifts to a large, round, glowing white disk set into the wall. The light is intense and almost featureless, surrounded by darkness. The man stands in silhouette in front of it, his head and shoulders black against the bright circle, before the view is overwhelmed by white glare. His face appears again, lit harshly from the side. His hair is pulled back but loose strands move around his face. He looks downward and then to the side, squinting and bracing himself against the brightness. The room keeps flashing between the blinding white light and the mechanical wall fixtures. The huge circular lamp dominates the left side of the space, while the man remains by the pedestal on the right, slightly hunched, as if under pressure from the light. On the wall, dark circular panels and recessed rings echo the shape of the lamp. One fixture resembles a black cone projecting straight out from a round opening. Another looks like a dark, rounded dome set into a circular frame. The man stands in profile near the pedestal, the giant white circle glowing behind him through a haze. Small wall markings or numerals are visible near the light, including characters that resemble “021,” and later large industrial-style numbers, including “26” and “27,” appear across a dark wall surface. These markings reinforce the chamber’s numbered, controlled atmosphere. The man’s posture remains tense. He looks off to one side, then turns, as if tracking something in the room or resisting instructions. In silhouette, he raises a hand toward the side of his head or ear, partially shielding himself. Brief, blurred glimpses of his face show him grimacing and narrowing his eyes; his eyes are shown extremely close, strained and searching under the glare. The white light swells again until it fills almost everything. When the man reappears, his face is clearer and more determined. He is still in the same loose shirt, standing against the gray wall and circular port behind him. He glances down, then turns his head sharply. Another pale circular shape fills the view, followed by another wash of white. His wrist and hand return in close detail. A smooth metal band is still around his wrist, and his hand moves quickly in the dark. He reaches toward an object and grasps what appears to be a pair of sunglasses: a compact, futuristic-looking frame with dark lenses and pale metallic parts. The product is handled as something he has retrieved for himself rather than something handed to him. Backlit by the enormous lamp, the man bends forward over the pedestal, almost swallowed by the glow. He raises his hands to his face and begins putting the sunglasses on. His body is a dark outline, shoulders rounded and head bowed, while the circular light burns behind him like a white sun. He holds the glasses in place, then gradually straightens. As he lifts his head, the light remains directly behind him, creating a halo around his silhouette. He stands more upright and still, no longer shielding his eyes with his hands. A bright white flash gives way to a detailed side profile of his face wearing the sunglasses. The Oakley-style eyewear is bold and sculptural: a silver or light gray wraparound frame with dark, rounded lenses. The frame has distinctive side panels around the eyes, including small circular holes near the lower edge, giving it a mechanical, protective look. The dark lenses cover his eyes completely, cutting the glare. His expression is calm and firm now, with his lips slightly parted in one moment and his jaw set. The product is shown close against his skin and hair, emphasizing the shape of the frame, the dark lens surface, and the way it shields his eyes. The commercial ends with the man again as a black silhouette, standing squarely before the large glowing circle. His shoulders are relaxed compared with earlier, and he faces the light directly. The chamber remains hazy and gray around him, but the sunglasses have changed his relationship to the glare: instead of recoiling or shielding himself, he stands still in front of it.

A waitress in a bright, retro-looking diner stands behind the counter holding a turquoise-blue box of Triples cereal upright so its front faces out. The box has large white “Triples” lettering, curved rainbow-like stripes, and a picture of golden cereal pieces near the bottom. The waitress is a light-skinned adult woman with short reddish-blonde hair, a pink headband, small hoop earrings, and a pink uniform dress with a white collar and white sleeve cuffs. Around her are shiny diner fixtures: shelves with dishes, a round glowing light or mirror behind her, metal appliances, and jars on the counter. Another worker in a similar pale pink uniform moves in the background. The waitress turns her head toward someone off to her left, leaning slightly over the counter with a confident, expectant expression while keeping the cereal box visible in front of her. Across the counter sit three customers in a booth-like diner setting with red seating, curtained windows, wall lights, and menus. In the center is a heavyset, middle-aged light-skinned man in a loose light-blue button-up shirt. A small white bowl sits in front of him. On his left is a younger-looking person with short dark hair, mostly hidden behind a menu; on his right is a blonde adult woman holding a large menu upright. Both side customers look calm and reserved while the man in the center looks straight ahead, expression flat and unimpressed. The commercial then moves into a clean product-comparison display on a plain white background. A blue Kellogg’s Rice Krispies box appears at the right, with large white “RICE KRISPIES” text and the familiar cartoon characters on the front. Along the bottom, small black legal text reads, “Rice Krispies is a registered trademark of the Kellogg Co.” A blue bowl filled with pale yellow cereal pieces slides into view on the left as the Rice Krispies box moves aside. Soon a second blue bowl appears to the right, filled with a darker golden cereal. A third blue bowl then rises into the foreground below them, filled with chunkier golden pieces. The three bowls arrange themselves like a triangle: two bowls higher in the background and one larger bowl lower in front. They then visually blend together into a single blue bowl filled with mixed golden cereal pieces, representing the combination in Triples. Back in the diner, the waitress rests her cheek on one hand behind the counter, watching with a small, knowing smile. Behind her are glass display cases and shelves with dishes and food items, softly lit in warm colors. The man in the blue shirt now eats from the bowl in front of him, with the Triples box standing on the counter to his left. He leans down over the bowl, takes a bite, and begins to react. His head dips, then he moves closer and closer, his face filling the view. His expression changes from concentration to surprise: his eyebrows lift, his eyes open wide, and he stares ahead with an exaggerated, comic look of discovery. The view widens again to the diner counter. The man has turned around on his stool, facing away from the counter toward the red booths behind him, as if doing a dramatic double take. The younger person and the blonde woman beside him remain mostly still behind their menus, while the Triples box, the bowl, a white mug, metal napkin holder, and condiment bottles sit along the counter. A brief layered transition shows the waitress over the diner scene, reinforcing that she is watching his reaction. She then appears close up, still in her pink uniform and headband, holding one hand near her face. She glances to the side with a satisfied, unsurprised expression, as though the man’s reaction is exactly what she expected. Finally, the three customers are shown together at the counter again. The Triples box stands prominently in the foreground on the left, front label facing out. The man in the blue shirt sits centered, smiling slightly now, with his bowl in front of him. The two people beside him continue holding menus, but their eyes angle toward him. The diner setting remains bright and orderly, with red booths, curtained windows, and counter items framing the product and the customer’s pleased reaction.

The commercial begins in a sleek, modern hotel lobby with polished floors, white walls, and a long reception counter glowing warmly from below. A man in a tan jacket and light trousers walks toward the front desk, pulling a small dark rolling suitcase behind him and carrying a shoulder bag. Other guests and staff move through the space: a suited man crosses the lobby on the left, a luggage cart stacked with dark bags stands to the right, and a uniformed hotel worker in a white shirt pushes it across the foreground. In the background are black metal stairs, framed artwork, tall windows, and a few people waiting or walking, giving the lobby a busy but upscale atmosphere. At the reception counter, the guest faces a male front-desk clerk. The clerk is a pale-skinned adult man with straight, chin-length black hair cut in a sharp bob. He wears a black suit jacket, a dark blue shirt, and a matching tie, with a small hoop earring visible in one ear. His expression is attentive and formal. The guest, a light-skinned adult man with short curly dark hair, wears an olive-tan blazer over a light blue button-up shirt. He stands slightly hunched over the counter, focused on the clerk, looking a little cautious or uncertain as he answers questions. The two men continue the check-in process. The guest leans in, looks down, and handles papers or a card on the counter. The clerk remains composed behind the desk, looking at him and occasionally looking down at the work surface. Behind them, a blonde woman in a bright pink top with a dark vest walks through the lobby, and other guests sit or pass by in the softly lit background. The guest reaches out across the counter, and the clerk extends his hand; they appear to exchange a small item, likely part of the check-in paperwork or room key. The guest then rests both hands near the edge of the counter and bends over, as if filling something out or signing. The clerk stands neatly on the opposite side, watching and waiting. As the conversation continues, the clerk’s face fills the view several times. He keeps steady eye contact with the guest and speaks with a polished, professional demeanor. His features are very still and controlled, and the curving branches of a potted plant behind him create a decorative shape over his shoulder. The guest, seen in return, looks up at the clerk with widened eyes, then glances down and to the side as if considering what he has just been offered. He seems to agree, then looks slightly hesitant but still cooperative. The scene shifts to a hotel bedroom. A red animated M&M’s character lies on his back on a white pillow, tucked on top of the bed linens like a person placed there for turn-down service. He is round and glossy red, with large white oval eyes, black pupils, a small smiling mouth, white gloves, and white shoes. A large white lowercase “m” is printed on the top of his candy shell. His arms are bent with gloved hands resting near his sides, and his legs are raised comfortably, making him look relaxed and expectant. A wider view reveals the red M&M on one side of a double bed, sharing the bed area with the human guest. The guest lies under white sheets and a dark blanket on the other side, his head on a pillow, wearing light-colored sleepwear. He is turned slightly toward the red M&M, looking uneasy or surprised by the candy character lying beside him. The room is warmly lit by matching bedside lamps on small wooden nightstands, with a wood headboard behind the pillows. The overall bedroom is cozy and dim, in contrast to the bright lobby. The red M&M remains positioned on the pillow beside the guest, visually turning the hotel’s “complimentary chocolate on your pillow” idea into a full-sized living candy character in bed.

Inside a dim Long John Silver’s dining area at night, three young male-presenting employees sit around a small table under a hanging lamp. They wear matching light blue polo shirts and black baseball caps with the restaurant logo. One employee on the left looks down quietly, while the one on the right faces the table with a tray of food in front of him. On the table are a yellow Long John Silver’s cup, a ketchup bottle, and a paper-lined basket of fried food. Across from the employees sits a small puppet-like character, about tabletop height, with a tan face, round staring eyes, wild bright red hair sticking out in all directions, and furry brown hands. The puppet is dressed formally in a black suit jacket, white shirt, and dark tie, as if being coached for a performance. The interaction focuses on the puppet and the employee seated opposite him. From over the employee’s shoulder, the puppet stands at the far side of the wooden table, facing him, while the food basket sits closer to the employee in the foreground. The puppet’s posture is alert and theatrical, with one hand on the table and its mouth moving as if trying to deliver a line. The young employee watches intently, his expression serious and instructive. The puppet reacts with exaggerated facial movements: its eyes widen, its mouth opens and closes, and its red hair flares around its head, making it look frantic and energetic. The food is then presented in a glossy, carefully arranged close-up against a dark background. A paper-lined basket holds several golden-brown breaded fish strips in the foreground, a large pile of pale golden fries rising along the back, two round fried hushpuppies on the right, a small clear cup of white tartar sauce on the left, and a sprig of green parsley tucked behind the sauce. Crumbs and crunchy bits are scattered beneath the fish strips, emphasizing the fried coating. The basket liner includes small Long John Silver’s logos along the edges. The food fills the screen more and more closely, showing the rough, crisp breading on the fish strips and hushpuppies and the smooth white sauce in the cup. The product arrangement widens to include a tall yellow drink cup standing behind the fries on the right. The cup is covered with visible condensation and has the colorful Long John Silver’s logo printed on it. The meal remains centered: fish strips across the front, fries fanning upward behind them, tartar sauce and parsley to the left, and hushpuppies to the right. The scene returns to the restaurant table. The employee is again seen facing the puppet, with the basket of food partly visible near the bottom edge of the table. The puppet, still in its black suit, looks up at him with wide eyes. The employee’s expression softens into a patient, slightly weary look as he appears to prompt the puppet again. The puppet opens its mouth very wide, as if finally attempting the line with great effort. In close-up, its eyes bulge and its red hair sticks out wildly while it leans forward over the table, mouth stretched open in an exaggerated shout or confession. Its body dips lower toward the tabletop, still facing the employee, looking overwhelmed by the food and the coaching. The commercial ends on a flat yellow background. Centered is the colorful Long John Silver’s logo. A moment later, black text appears beneath it reading, “HOW CAN YOU RESIST?”

On a busy city sidewalk outside a modern glass-fronted building, a young woman with shoulder-length brown hair stands at an outdoor flower stall. She wears a pale yellow-green dress under a black cardigan and smiles as she looks over bright bunches of pink and red flowers. On the display table beside her are a black handbag and a yellow Post Honey-Comb cereal box partly tucked into a white shopping bag. A young man in a black knit cap, red plaid shirt, dark gloves, and loose dark pants rushes in from behind her. He grabs the black handbag and the Honey-Comb box and bolts down the sidewalk. The woman’s expression changes to alarm; she turns, leans forward, and points after him. The thief sprints past benches outside the building, clutching the bright yellow cereal box against his chest. Several kids sit nearby. One blond boy, about early teen age, wears a red-and-black padded vest, elbow pads, wrist guards, and skater clothes, with a skateboard beside him. He looks up sharply, eyes widening in surprise. His face fills the view as he reacts with exaggerated amazement, then an animated green thought bubble appears above him, filled with giant golden Honey-Comb cereal pieces glistening with honey. He pulls on a yellow helmet decorated with dark spots and flame-like markings, as if inspired into action. The boy is suddenly represented as a small, wild-looking, furry cartoon character: yellow-orange shaggy fur, huge round eyes, a long pink nose and cheeks, black gloves, protective pads, and the same yellow helmet. He rides a skateboard down the sidewalk near parked bicycles and a flight of building steps. Arms out for balance, he gains speed, pops off the board, and leaps high, grinning broadly before landing back down in a chaotic slide. The thief, still hugging the Honey-Comb box, runs through a busier shopping area and looks back over his shoulder with a nervous grin. The furry skater pursues him along the sidewalk past stacks of newspapers. As the creature rushes through, the piles of papers fly apart, pages flipping and scattering across the pavement. Nearby dogs on leashes react and lunge; a large black-and-white dog fills the view as it jumps forward, while a smaller white dog stands beside it. Traffic passes in front of storefronts with red and green awnings. Water suddenly erupts in a tall white spray beside the street, and another column of golden cereal-like pieces or debris showers upward near a shop window, adding to the commotion. The thief pauses and turns his head, startled, then keeps running with the yellow box tight against his side. The chase continues past a green awning marked “K MARKET.” A large white animal figure or costume-like shape tumbles through the scene, and pedestrians in suits and casual clothes turn to watch. Ahead, two movers in blue coveralls are pushing a large black upright piano on a wheeled dolly along the sidewalk. The chaos barrels into them: the piano is struck or tipped, its wooden interior and strings exposed. A burst of dust and splinters fills the air. The furry skater shoots through the wreckage, then reappears with black-and-white piano keys comically jammed across his mouth like oversized teeth. He freezes for a beat with wide eyes and raised hands, looking dazed but still eager. The thief keeps moving, clutching the Honey-Comb box. He runs past a construction area where orange-and-white striped barriers and steam mark an open manhole.
