He presses a plank flat with his hands, smiles down at his work, and then uses a small yellow-and-black rubber mallet to tap a piece into place, aligning the flooring. A phone screen then shows a Home Depot delivery option. A tile with a small truck icon reads “Scheduled Delivery,” and a finger presses it; the tile turns orange to indicate it has been selected. Outside a house, a Home Depot delivery worker wearing a dark cap, dark shirt, khaki pants, and a white face mask carries a cardboard box. The box has The Home Depot logo and the printed slogan, “How doers get more done.” Other Home Depot boxes are stacked inside the open back of a delivery truck, whose side also bears the orange logo. The worker brings the box to a front porch with a wooden door, blue shutters, potted plants, and a white rocking chair. A woman in a pink top and blue jeans steps forward and picks up the delivered Home Depot box. From inside the open box, the woman and a young girl look down into it. The girl, with long braided hair and a striped shirt, watches as the woman reaches in and lifts out packaged parts. In a bathroom with bright windows, a white sink, and a large mirror, the woman begins installing a shiny chrome faucet. Seen partly through reflections, she leans over the sink, focused and smiling slightly as she positions the fixture. A product box nearby is labeled “Rubicon” and “THE BOLD LOOK OF KOHLER,” indicating a Kohler faucet. She steadies the faucet body with one hand and adjusts it into place on the sink. The woman who was painting earlier reappears in the sunlit room, now with the wall fully painted a rich orange-brown. She pulls up and drags away a large section of old carpet or padding, exposing the wood floor beneath. The material billows as she yanks it across the room, then collapses toward the floor as she continues clearing the space. In the finished bathroom, the woman in the pink top and the young girl stand together at the white sink. Both smile and laugh as the girl reaches toward the new chrome faucet, apparently testing the water. Their reflections are visible in the mirror, along with countertop accessories such as a soap dispenser and toothbrush holders. The commercial ends on a clean white screen with a small orange Home Depot logo centered.

A bright, cozy living room is set up for a home assembly project. Two young adults kneel on a white shag rug around a low white coffee table with pale wooden legs. The man, on the left, wears a brown jacket and dark pants; the woman, on the right, wears a dark blue button-up shirt and a colorful headband holding back curly dark hair. Behind them are large sunlit windows, a brick wall, a tan sofa with a yellow blanket, cardboard boxes, framed pictures leaning against the wall, and small tools scattered on the rug. They are looking at the table and the instruction papers, as if finishing the build. The woman studies a large folded instruction sheet while holding a small white part in one hand. The man, still kneeling, reaches toward the table. A purple drink can sits on the glossy white tabletop. As he adjusts or moves the table, the surface tilts sharply, and the can begins to slide across it. A close view shows the purple can tipped on its side on the white tabletop, its open pull tab visible. The woman reacts with alarm. She faces forward with her mouth open wide, eyes enlarged, one hand raised like a stop signal and the instruction paper flying upward beside her. The paper lands on the rug, where the printed page is visible with the bold heading “Instructions,” small diagrams of the table, and a simple cartoon-like figure holding tools. A pinkish-purple streak of spilled liquid appears on the tabletop nearby. A roll of Bounty paper towels is quickly placed upright on the white table by an arm in a rolled-up blue sleeve. The roll has a bright green label with the large “Bounty” logo and the phrase “The Quicker Picker Upper” printed beneath it. The spill remains visible as a long pink-purple smear on the tabletop to the right of the roll. A hand presses a folded white Bounty paper towel onto the purple spill. The towel is thick and bright white, and the hand smooths it firmly across the glossy surface. As the towel moves over the liquid, the purple streak shortens and lightens, being drawn into the towel. Small disclaimer text appears near the bottom of the image. Large white-and-purple on-screen words build over the cleaned surface: “absorbs like a sponge,” with “sponge” shown in large purple letters. By the time the towel lifts away, the tabletop underneath looks clean, while the towel has absorbed the purple liquid. The commercial then shows a side-by-side comparison on a plain white surface. On the left, a hand uses a sheet labeled by nearby on-screen text as the “Leading Ordinary Brand”; on the right, another hand uses a Bounty towel, with the Bounty logo displayed near the lower right. Both hands press towels into separate purple puddles. The ordinary-brand sheet on the left becomes heavily soaked and dark purple, and when it is lifted, a visible drop of purple liquid falls back down, leaving liquid behind. On the right, the Bounty towel also turns purple where it has absorbed the spill, but it is handled in a thicker folded pad and continues wiping the surface. The Bounty side shows the hand sweeping the towel across the remaining small pink puddle until the surface looks clear. Fine print along the bottom mentions flavored sparkling water and indicates a time-lapse comparison. The final scene shifts to a clean, softly lit kitchen-like counter. A bright green spill lies spread across the white surface in the foreground. A roll of Bounty drops down upright directly onto the green liquid, standing in the middle of the puddle. Its white roll and green Bounty label face forward, with the “Bounty” name and “The Quicker Picker Upper” slogan visible. A small blue P&G logo appears in the upper right corner as the roll sits on the spill, surrounded by the vivid green liquid.

A couple sits on a light-colored sofa in a bright, tidy living room that opens into a white kitchen. The man, with curly dark hair and a full beard, wears a green long-sleeve polo and dark pants; he holds a small black remote in his right hand and faces the television. Beside him, a woman with short dark hair wears a dark patterned blouse and blue jeans, sitting curled up with one leg tucked under her and her hand near her face. A blue patterned pillow rests to the man’s side, and on the coffee table in front of them are a bowl of chips and a pale drink in a glass. Both look focused on what they are watching. Their television sits within a white built-in wall unit with shelves holding books, vases, and decorative objects. On the screen, a Black woman tennis player in a dark athletic outfit appears in action on a tennis court, then the image changes to Wonder Woman standing in a sunlit mall-like atrium with white columns and a glass ceiling. The TV alternates between the tennis player preparing a shot and Wonder Woman in her red, gold, and blue armor. Glowing golden lasso-like streaks sweep across Wonder Woman, and the images begin to visually merge. The screen darkens, then a glowing outline forms around a figure holding a tennis racket. The figure resolves into Serena Williams dressed as Wonder Woman: gold headpiece, red-and-gold armored bodice, blue skirt, silver bracers, and a tennis racket held like a weapon. She stands in the middle of a busy, polished indoor shopping mall. The couple reacts from the couch, still facing forward, the man lifting the remote slightly. On the TV, the mall scene expands into a playful battle. Several spider-like machines move across the shiny floor. They have multiple jointed legs, blue and green mechanical bodies, clear domes filled with bright yellow tennis balls, red lights, and cannon-like tubes. They scuttle through the atrium near stairs, planters, café tables, and passersby. On an escalator, an elderly white-haired woman in a cream outfit grips the railing while a man in sunglasses and a tan sweater recoils beside her. A tennis ball bounces near them, and both appear startled. Serena, as Wonder Woman, watches intensely, her face framed by wavy light-brown hair and the gold headband. Her expression is serious and focused. A green tennis-ball robot creeps near a planter while people in the background hurry away. Nearby, an older white-haired man in a white tennis polo with a blue stripe and white shorts—visually resembling John McEnroe—stands among café chairs holding an orange tray. He looks down at the tray as red sauce or food dangles messily from it, then looks up with a strained, incredulous expression. Serena’s face returns in close view, steady and stern. One blue-and-white-legged robot positions itself on a stair landing and launches a tennis ball from its clear ball chamber. Serena lunges into action in the mall café area, racket in hand. She twists her body, swings powerfully, and strikes back. Her costume’s gold and red armor catches the warm mall lighting, while rows of small ceiling lights form a dotted pattern above her. The returned ball slams into a robot near the stairs. The machine bursts apart in a bright spray of sparks, scattering dozens of yellow tennis balls and mechanical pieces across the floor. Serena turns and continues swinging, looking over her shoulder as more robots and tennis balls move through the mall. From a low angle near her boots, another green robot is hit near a cluster of plants; sparks fly, smoke rises, and parts skid across the glossy floor while people and additional robots remain in the background. The action is then seen again on the couple’s television within the white shelving unit. Serena, still dressed as Wonder Woman, leans forward on the screen, then swings her racket as a tennis ball flies past. Large white text appears over the TV image, building to the slogan “GET YOUR TV TOGETHER” across the center-left of the screen. The commercial returns to the couple on the sofa. Both remain seated in the same living room, watching with wide, absorbed expressions, the man still holding the remote and the woman leaning in with her hand near her face.

An adult man stands in a bright living room, holding and folding a soft grey item, possibly laundry. He has short dark curly hair, a goatee, and wears a light grey sweater with grey pants. Around him are a blue sofa with patterned and yellow pillows, houseplants, framed wall art, shelves, and a staircase with a gallery wall, giving the room a warm family-home feel. A young girl appears in another sunlit area of the home, near a glass-paned door and children’s storage shelves. She has dark hair in two braids and wears denim overalls over a striped long-sleeve shirt, a red backpack, bracelets, and white sneakers with colourful accents. She walks through the room dragging a floppy, beige stuffed bunny by one ear or paw. Close to the floor, the plush toy trails along the wood floor beside her shoes, its long ears and soft body brushing the ground as she steps forward. The girl lifts the stuffed bunny up to her face and presses it against her mouth and nose, cuddling it closely with both hands. Her eyes peek over the toy. The man is then seen in close-up, looking alert and concerned, as if he has noticed the toy being dragged and then hugged. Back in the living room, the girl smiles and swings the stuffed bunny forward. The man suddenly lunges across the room in an exaggerated protective pose, arms spread wide and body stretched out horizontally, as if diving to intercept the toy. Large bold white words appear across the scene: “PROTECT MODE.” The phrase stays on screen as he flies past the blue sofa, mouth open and eyes wide, reaching toward the plush bunny at the right side of the room. The moment is playful and dramatic, with the father presented like a superhero reacting to a possible mess or germ risk. The man lands back in motion holding the stuffed bunny, while the girl’s arm remains outstretched from the right side of the room. A small line of text appears near the bottom: “Use as directed.” The bunny is dropped into a white laundry basket filled with clothes. Inside the basket, a white bottle with a blue cap is visible among the fabrics. The label identifies it as Lysol Laundry Sanitizer, with “0% Bleach” visible on the front. The product is then shown more clearly on a laundry-room counter. A hand holds the white Lysol Laundry Sanitizer bottle upright, label facing forward. The bottle has a rounded shape, a blue cap, and a blue-and-white label with the Lysol logo and “Laundry Sanitizer” prominently displayed. A pale yellow laundry bottle sits blurred in the background. The stuffed bunny appears inside a front-loading washing machine, surrounded by light-coloured laundry. The man’s hand closes the round glass door, leaving the bunny visible through the window at the center. The “Use as directed” text remains near the bottom. The man then stands beside the washer with the Lysol Laundry Sanitizer bottle on the counter and the blue cap in his other hand, suggesting he is adding it to the laundry routine. After washing, the girl sits on the blue sofa holding the stuffed bunny close to her chest. She smiles broadly, then squeezes the bunny in a hug, looking happy and comfortable. The living room background remains softly lit, with the staircase and wall art behind her. The commercial ends with a product display on a white surface: two bottles of Lysol Laundry Sanitizer with blue caps stand side by side, one larger and one smaller. A red label above the smaller bottle reads “NEW TRIAL SIZE.” Large white text on the right says, “TRY FOR UNDER $5.”

The commercial opens on a white flag with a turquoise stripe along the bottom, fluttering against a bright blue sky. In bold dark letters across the flag is the Orbitz name and logo. The scene shifts to a sunny beach: a slim, shirtless young man with light skin, curly dark hair, and a small mustache stands near the shoreline with his hands on his hips. A small open-air cart drives along a narrow road lined with trees and dense greenery. A middle-aged Black woman with voluminous curly hair sits upright in the back seat, facing forward. She wears a patterned pink top, red pants, sandals, bracelets, and holds a large woven bag beside her. The cart has red upholstery and decorative red elements hanging from its roof. A driver in white is partly visible in front. On the roadside to the right is a green sign with white writing, including the word “VYTILLA.” On the left, a few people stand near the road, one lifting an object above his head as the cart passes. Inside a cozy ski-lodge-like room, two adults in winter gear stand near a row of skis. One, presenting as male, wears a red jacket, black pants, ski goggles pushed up on his head, and has one hand on his hip. Beside him, another adult presenting as female wears a gray-and-white plaid ski jacket, white snow pants, a green hood or hat, purple earflaps or hair framing the face, glasses, and holds a pair of skis upright. Behind them are large windows looking out onto snowy mountains, wooden walls, snowshoes, skis, and lodge furnishings. Other people sit or stand in the background, bundled for winter. At a modern tropical resort, an older Black man stands shirtless on an upper balcony beside a glass railing. He wears a dark sarong or wrap skirt with a large floral pattern. Below him is a turquoise swimming pool, white hotel balconies, lounge chairs, umbrellas, palm trees, and bright sun. A closer view shows the floral wrap tied at his waist and his hand resting confidently on his hip. Then his face is seen more clearly: he is bald with a gray beard, looking steady and self-assured, with lush greenery and blue sky behind him. In a hotel bedroom, a young couple lies side by side under a dark blanket on a large bed with a tufted cream headboard. The young man, in light blue pajamas, lies on his back looking toward the young woman. The young woman, in a pale patterned pajama top, lies beside him, turned slightly toward him, her hands resting over the blanket. The room is softly lit, with a bedside table and lamp visible. A wider view of the same bed shows the covers rising into a tent-like mound over the middle of the mattress, while the rest of the room remains neat and symmetrical, with lamps on both sides and a service tray or drinks table to the right. On a bright outdoor terrace overlooking the ocean, two people relax in separate square wooden soaking tubs. A man sits in the left tub with his arms draped over the rim, smiling toward the woman in the right tub. The woman, wearing sunglasses and a head covering, smiles back from her own tub. Large potted tropical plants frame the scene, and the sea stretches out beyond a low wall. Beside a resort pool, an elderly woman reclines on a turquoise-cushioned lounge chair. She has light skin, a blonde beehive-like hairstyle or wrapped hair, oversized white round sunglasses, large earrings, and a pale pink flowing cover-up over a decorative swimsuit or necklace. Her legs are stretched out, and she appears relaxed and amused. The pool water gleams beside her, with palm trees, white umbrellas, and the ocean in the background. A person in white walks near the pool behind her, carrying cleaning or pool equipment. A closer view shows her smiling slightly from behind the large white sunglasses. Back in the ski lodge, the two winter-dressed adults stand closer to the foreground, facing forward. The person in the red jacket stands solidly with one hand on the hip; the person in the plaid jacket holds skis upright at their side. Their expressions are calm and resolved, with racks of skis and wooden wall panels behind them. The beach scene returns to the slim young man in striped swim briefs. Now he lifts a pair of reflective sunglasses to his face with one hand. The white lighthouse rises blurred behind him, and the sunlit beach and blue umbrellas remain in the background. The elderly woman at the pool appears again in profile on her lounge chair, still wearing her white sunglasses and looking relaxed, with the ocean and a pool worker behind her. A wide green golf course appears, lined with tall palm trees and dotted with sand traps. Two golfers stand on the fairway near a small golf cart. One golfer, a light-skinned man wearing a white shirt, yellow argyle sweater vest, blue pants, cap, sunglasses, and a golf glove, holds a smartphone in one hand while a golf club rests nearby. Another golfer stands behind him in a blue-and-red top and tan pants, watching. A close view shows the smartphone in the golfer’s hand. The Orbitz mobile app is open, with the Orbitz logo at the top and a list of hotel options displayed below, including small hotel photos, star ratings, and prices. A thumb scrolls or taps the screen. The display changes to a hotel detail page with a photo of a bedroom at the top, text beneath it, and a prominent blue action button near the lower right, suggesting a booking step. The final scene returns to the golf course. The golfer in the argyle vest stands on the fairway holding a flagpole with a blue Orbitz flag. The flag flutters in the open air among tall palm trees, green grass, and bright sun, echoing the opening image of the Orbitz-branded flag.

The commercial opens above a sunny beach, looking straight down at pale sand, foamy surf, and several colorful umbrellas casting round shadows. A lone person walks near the waterline, while beach towels and umbrellas are spread below. On the sand beside a bright pink towel, a pair of bare feet presses and buries the toes into a little mound of sand. An orange flying disc lies nearby, and another person’s legs approach in the background, making the toe-hiding gesture feel deliberate. The setting shifts to a bright, tidy living room with a large brown leather sofa, a coffee table, and a white kitchen in the background. An adult man in a green T-shirt and rolled-up jeans sits sideways on the couch with his knees bent. A white bulldog lies beside him, droopy-faced, on the same sofa cushion. As another adult, partly visible at the left edge, stands nearby in jeans and flip-flops, the man slides his bare feet back toward the dog and the sofa cushions, tucking them out of easy view. By a swimming pool, the view is from someone reclining on a white slatted lounge chair. Their bare feet point toward the pool, then curl and pull inward under the chair’s front slats as a person in black flip-flops walks past on the brick pool deck. In a garden, a bare foot in a dark flip-flop steps onto a coiled green hose lying in the grass, pressing the toes down among the loops. In a yoga or exercise studio, a bare foot beside a green mat nudges the edge of a blue mat upward and slips the toes underneath it, again hiding them. A clean white background introduces the product imagery. A pair of bare feet rests on the white surface, with small on-screen text along the bottom reading, “Prescription KERYDIN (tavaborole) is FDA-approved,” and the Kerydin logo at the lower right. A hand brings in a small applicator dropper and lowers it toward a big toenail, positioning the tip as if to apply liquid medication. The view then moves very close to the toenails; on one large toenail, the words “TOENAIL FUNGUS” appear written in rough, dark letters. At the bottom, small text explains that Kerydin drops are used once daily for 48 weeks on affected toenails only, and that it can take a year or more to grow a healthy toenail. Back on the beach, several adults lie on turquoise striped towels arranged like spokes in a circle, their feet pointing inward toward the center. Some are in swimsuits or light beach clothing, and the sand around them is textured with footprints. A white band across the bottom carries safety text: “KERYDIN may cause irritation at the treated site,” with the Kerydin logo on the right. The scene changes to a yoga class in a warm orange-walled studio. Adults sit or stand on mats with their arms raised overhead. A bearded adult man in a gray shirt smiles slightly as he stretches, with other participants close beside him. The lower white band now lists common side effects, including skin peeling, ingrown toenail, redness, itching, and swelling. The focus drops to a row of bare feet lined up on green and blue yoga mats, the participants standing evenly spaced on a wooden floor while the same side-effect text remains visible. Outdoors again, at a sunny backyard gathering, the view stays low at foot level. Bare feet and flip-flopped feet cross a strip of green grass in front of a patio, flowerpots, and a grill. People in summer clothing move casually through the yard; one person in a rust-colored skirt steps forward in flat sandals, while others stand or pass in the background. The bottom text reads, “Individual results may vary,” with the Kerydin logo still at the lower right. Two people’s feet face each other on the grass, suggesting a social moment, with one person in dark pants and black flip-flops opposite the person in the skirt and sandals. The yoga studio returns briefly. A man seated cross-legged on a green mat lifts one bare foot high near his head, holding the ankle with one hand, while a woman beside him sits upright on her mat in a calm pose. Shelves behind them hold rolled yoga mats in different colors. A small note at the bottom says, “See our ad in People,” alongside the Kerydin logo. Near the end, a pair of bare feet rests together under a white sheet on a bed. The toes are visible at first, nestled against the sheet, then the white bedding slides down and covers them completely, leaving only soft folds of fabric filling the screen. Over the white fabric, the Kerydin droplet logo appears, followed by a small bottle and applicator cap beside the product name. The final screen reads “Kerydin (tavaborole) topical solution, 5%,” with the product bottle on the left and the Kerydin name large in blue. At the bottom, the visible contact line says, “Visit www.TOETUCKER.com or call 1-844-KERYDIN for product information.”

The man looks up at her with a surprised, slightly uncertain expression while his friends watch from either side. The blonde woman bends nearer, her body crossing the foreground as she reaches toward him. The young man glances sideways at one of his friends, looking hesitant. She takes hold of him or draws him by the arm, and he stretches his arm out awkwardly as if being pulled away from the safety of the table. His expression tightens into a nervous look as he rises. They arrive near the pool table, where colorful billiard balls sit scattered on the green felt. Other young women stand and dance nearby, including a dark-haired woman in an orange tank top holding or standing near a pool cue. The blonde woman positions the young man in the open space beside the pool table. She faces him with a small, expectant smile, while he stands stiffly with his green beer bottle in hand. The blonde starts to dance in front of him, shoulders and arms moving lightly. He responds with an awkward, cautious attempt: holding the Rolling Rock bottle in one hand, he raises his other hand near his head and makes small, uncertain fist-pumping motions. His posture is stiff and self-conscious. The blonde watches him closely, then glances aside as if measuring his effort. Around them, other patrons continue drinking, dancing, and watching from tables. His three male friends are shown at their table, leaning forward with beers in front of them. One wears a coral-pink shirt, another a dark shirt, and another a tan shirt. They stare toward him with amused, intent expressions, surrounded by green bottles and a snack bowl. Back on the dance floor, the man and the blonde stand facing each other. He holds his beer low and gestures with his hands, as if explaining or trying to excuse himself. She keeps a composed, assessing expression, occasionally lifting her hands in small dance-like motions. He begins to smile, looking more comfortable, and turns his attention off to one side. A second blonde young woman approaches from nearby, wearing a burgundy sleeveless top with light trim and her hair pulled back in a ponytail. She holds green Rolling Rock bottles, and a small tray with more bottles is visible between her and the man. The man reaches toward the bottles and takes them. The Rolling Rock labels are visible on the green glass as the bottles cluster together near chest height. The ponytailed woman smiles faintly while handing them over. The man looks down at the two bottles now in front of him, his face becoming blank and thoughtful for a moment. Across the room, his three friends grin broadly. One lifts a green bottle toward him in a silent toast while the others smile and gesture, clearly pleased with themselves. The man looks back up, now smiling with a slightly sheepish, knowing expression. The blonde woman in the black top reappears behind him, smiling too, and places a hand lightly on his shoulder. As they stand together, the Rolling Rock horse-head logo and ribbon graphic fade over them, followed by the white words “KEEP ON ROCKIN’” on the green, condensation-covered bottle glass. The commercial ends on another close view of the Rolling Rock label, with the blue “ROLLING ROCK” name and “Extra Pale” text prominent on the wet green bottle.

A group of children and early teenagers appears on a glossy stage, all dressed in shiny silver outfits that look futuristic and performance-oriented: loose metallic pants, silver tops, hats or bucket-style caps, and bright white or silver shoes. The stage has a reddish-orange floor, a copper-colored draped curtain at the back, and black side walls marked with thin horizontal light lines. The kids dance in formation, with one boy in front dropping low and sliding into breakdance-style moves while the others pose and wave their arms behind him. Their expressions are energetic and playful. A girl in the center then holds up a clapperboard-style sign with visible red “pop-tarts” lettering and bold black words reading “BREAKFAST CREW.” The other kids crowd around the sign, leaning toward the viewer and smiling as if introducing themselves as a team. The setting changes to a bright, stylized breakfast room with a green-and-blue checkerboard floor, blue walls, and a round black table. The children, still in metallic silver outfits, gather around the table. On the tabletop are yellow plates, glasses of orange juice, and a small vase of yellow flowers. They gesture and dance while seated and standing, raising their hands and waving small white rectangular objects that appear to be Pop-Tarts. A strong white light floods the room, and the children move away from the table as the space becomes hazy and glowing. In the blue-lit room beyond, the table remains in the foreground with place settings and orange juice, while the children dance in the background. The room then becomes almost dreamlike: bright white light, confetti-like speckles on the floor, and a large shiny chrome object shaped like an oversized toaster or toaster cage hangs or sits at the center while the silver-clad children dance around it. The children continue dancing in a gray, futuristic room with a wall of square light panels. Their metallic outfits catch the light, and the group moves in synchronized, bouncy steps. Close-ups show individual children smiling and moving their arms toward the viewer. The product is then shown directly: rectangular Pop-Tarts float against a colorful satin-like background of orange, blue, green, and pink fabric. One pastry has pink frosting with a darker pink spiral pattern; another has glossy chocolate frosting with white speckles; another has white frosting covered with multicolored sprinkles. The pastries are shown as flat, four-sided rectangles with golden pastry edges and brightly decorated tops. The action shifts to a blue-and-black studio-like space filled with oversized silver exercise balls and large display panels showing toaster graphics. A boy in a silver bucket hat stands in front, holding a small silver toaster-like object against his chest while dancing. Other children bounce or sit on the silver balls behind him, raising their arms and moving in rhythm. The room has a futuristic playground feel, with shiny floors, suspended metal framework overhead, and repeated images of toasters on the panels. A girl with pigtails and fluffy purple hair ties appears in close-up, smiling as she holds a frosted Pop-Tart with both hands and bites into it. Her eyes close briefly as she eats. A round, metallic appliance sits open like a drawer or turntable, with several frosted pastry pieces arranged in circular positions. The visible flavors include pink-frosted, chocolate-frosted, white-sprinkled, and purple-frosted designs. A silver-sleeved hand places a white-frosted pastry into one of the spaces. The children gather around the appliance, leaning in with excited faces. The machine has blue knobs, small indicator lights, a central dome on top, and red glowing fins or vents on the side, making it look like a playful sci-fi toaster station. The children smile, point, and raise their arms as if reacting to the pastries being prepared. Back in the blue studio with the silver balls, the children bounce and dance on the large spheres, leaning forward toward the viewer and pumping their arms. Then the perspective shifts overhead: several children look upward from a floor scattered with blue confetti. They hold Pop-Tarts and pieces of pastry close to their mouths. One girl at the left takes a bite, a boy in the center holds a frosted piece, and another child in a white hat holds a dark pastry. They crowd together from below, looking up with wide, excited expressions while continuing to eat. A close-up of a large black speaker cone fills the screen, followed by a product display set in a room whose walls are covered with many circular speakers. On a small tabletop are a Kellogg’s Pop-Tarts box, a blue plate holding broken Pop-Tarts with visible purple filling, a tall glass of orange juice, and a smaller glass of milk. The box shows the red Kellogg’s logo and the Pop-Tarts branding, with large purple “Wild!” lettering and berry-themed graphics. Small copyright text appears near the bottom left, while the product is arranged like part of a breakfast setting. The children return in another blue futuristic room with big black circular speakers on the walls. A girl in the foreground wears large silver-and-red headphones and a shiny silver top with dark feathery trim at the cuffs. Rectangular Pop-Tarts and small pastry pieces float or fly around her. She reaches toward a Pop-Tart, brings it to her mouth, and takes a bite, closing her eyes briefly as she chews. Behind her, other silver-clad children dance and throw their arms up. More Pop-Tarts pass through the air around them, reinforcing the sense of a loud, active, playful breakfast party. The commercial ends on a wide view of a large blue sci-fi stage. The children dance together at the center beneath tall curved arches, with black circular speakers built into the walls on both sides. Dozens of rectangular Pop-Tarts or pastry-like pieces drift through the air all around them like confetti. The group keeps moving in coordinated poses, some crouching and others raising their arms. The setting pulls back visually to reveal the whole stage enclosed inside a transparent rounded dome, flanked by huge headphone-like shapes on either side, as if the entire breakfast crew is performing inside an oversized futuristic sound chamber.

A warm, staged talk-show set is visible, with a seated studio audience on the left applauding and a television camera crew on the right. The set has tan wall panels, a brick column, potted greenery, two dark upholstered armchairs, and a small wooden coffee table with blue mugs. Blue-and-white signs on the walls read “Ryan Moore.” A middle-aged white male host with gray hair, glasses, and a light blue long-sleeved polo shirt stands near a Black woman seated in one of the armchairs. She wears a bright pink top, black pants, small hoop earrings, a watch, and a chunky bracelet. A lower-third graphic appears over the scene with the “Ryan Moore” logo and the title “DUPED MOMS.” The host leans in toward the woman, holding a black handheld microphone close to her. In a close view, she looks upset and animated, her eyebrows raised and her mouth open as she speaks. She holds a crumpled white tissue near her chin and gestures with her hand, at times pointing outward and then turning her palm up as if explaining something emotional or frustrating. The brick wall behind her gives the moment a staged talk-show interview feel. The host watches her closely, keeping the microphone near her mouth. The host then faces forward and gestures broadly with his free hand, as if calling someone onto the stage. Two large white chicken-like characters enter from the side near the “Ryan Moore” sign. They are human-sized, scruffy, feather-covered mascots with long yellow legs, oversized yellow beaks, and floppy wings. One is taller and broader; the other is shorter and thinner. They shuffle onto the set between the armchairs. The woman in pink is shown with her arms folded, leaning back with a skeptical, displeased expression as the birds appear. From the studio floor, the two feathered characters face the audience and crew, their beaks open as if talking. Overhead studio lights, equipment, seated audience members, and crew are visible behind them, emphasizing that this is a talk-show taping. The host stands off to the right in the set area. The two chicken characters are then seated in the dark armchairs, their long yellow legs stretched awkwardly toward the floor and their wings resting over the chair arms. The small wooden table with blue mugs sits between them and the host. The host stands in front of them, holding the microphone, while the birds look up at him. The host appears to challenge them, then turns away with a knowing smile and makes a sweeping gesture, as if introducing evidence. A large wall monitor behind the seating area now displays a home-video-style scene. In that inset scene, a toddler with dark hair sits in a wooden high chair at a dining table in a dim dining room. Beside the child is one of the scruffy white chicken characters. A large disposable cup with a straw rests near the child, and the chicken character holds a blue aerosol-style can. The child has white foam or cream around the mouth while looking toward the bird. The chicken leans close, the blue can and the large cup crowding the high-chair tray, creating the impression of the bird feeding or spraying something messy to the toddler. Back on the talk-show set, the two chicken characters sit stiffly in their chairs beneath the “Ryan Moore” sign, looking exposed. The woman in pink suddenly reacts. She twists in her chair, plants her hands on the armrests, and pushes herself up with a shocked, angry expression. In the wide view, the monitor behind her still shows the toddler with foam around the mouth. The host stands to the right watching, his arms partly folded. The woman rushes across the stage toward the seated birds. She bends over the smaller chicken character and grabs at it, pushing into the bird’s feathery body while the larger one slumps nearby. A crew member and camera are visible at the far right as the confrontation spills across the talk-show set. The scene then changes to a close-up of cooked food: glossy strips of chicken mixed with sliced onions and red, orange, and green bell peppers. Steam rises from the hot food, and the chicken and vegetables glisten as they sit piled together, suggesting a freshly cooked fajita-style meal. Over the food, the Foster Farms logo fades in: a yellow rectangular label with a red square containing a white chicken silhouette, next to the words “Foster Farms.” Beneath it, white text reads, “Always natural. Always fresh.”

The scene opens in a dim kitchen at night, seen from near floor level. An open refrigerator glows on the left, casting cool white-blue light across the shiny floor. Inside the fridge are shelves with jars and containers, and on the floor nearby are scattered items, including small round objects and what looks like spilled food or packaging. Wooden cabinets line the right side, and an orange hanging lamp glows above a table in the background. The room feels quiet and slightly mysterious, with deep shadows and a bluish nighttime atmosphere. Attention shifts to a round kitchen table under the orange lamp. At the center sits a dark bowl on a rectangular bamboo-style placemat. The bowl is filled with Reese’s candy: bright orange wrapped bars and loose candy pieces in orange, yellow, and brown. Around the table are everyday objects, including papers or folders, a mug, and small condiment shakers, but the bowl of candy is the brightest and most prominent object. The light from the lamp creates a circular pool of illumination around it while the edges of the kitchen remain dark. The bowl is then seen closer, filled to the rim with Reese’s products. A large orange wrapper with the yellow Reese’s logo rises above the loose candy pieces. Other orange wrappers are tucked around it, and the candy pieces gleam against the dark bowl. The kitchen background is blurred and shadowy, with the table and the candy sharply emphasized. A closer view of a Reese’s package shows the label clearly: “Reese’s” and “2 Peanut Butter Cups” on the orange wrapper. Loose Reese’s Pieces in orange, yellow, and brown appear around it, as if the candies are clustered and beginning to move or swirl. A product display appears against the same cool kitchen background. Several Reese’s packages are arranged upright like a group portrait on a textured blue surface. Visible products include Reese’s Pieces, ReeseSticks, Reese’s Bites, Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups Miniatures, NutRageous, and a standard Reese’s 2 Peanut Butter Cups bar in front. All the packaging is mainly bright orange with yellow and brown branding. Along the bottom, small white text explains the free-ticket offer: free tickets by mail with proofs of purchase from three bags or twelve candy bars, requests received by 8/1/02, six to eight weeks for delivery, up to six tickets per household, and details available at in-store displays. A yellow ticket slides into view on the right with large black text reading “FREE MOVIE TICKET,” visually connecting the candy purchase to the movie-ticket promotion. The scene returns to the kitchen, where loose Reese’s Pieces and wrapped candies fly through the air in a stream. Orange, yellow, and brown pieces arc across the room, along with small wrapped candies. They move in a long, curving trail, passing in front of cabinets and the kitchen counter. E.T., the small brown alien character, is now visible in the kitchen. He has a wrinkled, leathery face, a long thin neck, large wide-set eyes, and a small body with narrow shoulders. He stands upright in the foreground, looking toward the flying candy with a calm, curious expression. The candies continue to sail past E.T. in slow, graceful arcs. Some pass close to his face, and a few appear to drift toward his mouth. Behind him are wooden cabinets, a sink beneath a window with closed blinds, curtains, and countertop items such as a red bowl and kitchen utensils. E.T.’s head turns slightly as he watches the colorful pieces move around him. His large eyes follow the candies, and his mouth forms a small, pleased smile. A few candies hover directly in front of E.T.’s face, then one reaches his mouth. He appears to eat or taste it, his expression softening into satisfaction. He raises one long, thin finger beside his face. The fingertip begins to glow with a warm yellow-white light, standing out against the dark kitchen. Small Reese’s Pieces continue to drift behind and near him, their orange and yellow colors echoing the glow at the end of his finger. E.T. looks at the glowing fingertip with quiet focus, as if his familiar glowing touch has been sparked by the candy moment. The final image is a simple brand card: the word “Reese’s” in large yellow script with a dark outline, centered on a warm orange background. The logo remains steady and uncluttered, ending the sequence with the Reese’s name filling the screen.

In a bright, tidy living room, a person is partly visible at the right edge, seen from the waist down in pale pink pants and light shoes. They guide a full-size upright vacuum with a blue bag across a tan carpet. The room has a soft, domestic look: a pale blue armchair sits near curtained windows, a beige sofa is behind a wooden coffee table with decorative objects, and shelves and plants fill the background. The upright vacuum is then replaced visually by a compact red handheld vacuum, held out in the person’s hand by its top handle, with its black power cord trailing behind. A small, fluffy white dog lies on a pale blue upholstered chair or sofa cushion. The red handheld vacuum rests nearby at the left. As the dog moves off the cushion, patches of light-colored hair or debris are left scattered across the fabric. A hand brings the red Dirt Devil hand vac onto the cushion and pushes it steadily over the mess. The compact vacuum has a rounded red body, a top handle, a black front intake opening, small side vents, and a red soft-looking dust bag at the rear. As it passes over the blue fabric, the visible clumps of hair and dirt disappear beneath the nozzle, leaving the surface cleaner. The vacuum is then shown upright in close detail with its underside facing forward. A metal-framed opening reveals two cylindrical brush areas inside the head. The view centers on the revolving brush mechanism, with bristles visible behind the gray rollers, highlighting that this handheld cleaner has a brush like a larger upright vacuum. The setting changes to the inside of a car. The red hand vac is positioned on a gray car seat where dark crumbs or dirt are scattered along the seat seam. A person in pink clothing holds the vacuum while also using a white hose and narrow attachment. White on-screen text at the lower left reads “Attachments Available.” The hose attachment is aimed into the tight spaces between the car seat and center area, suggesting cleaning in narrow crevices. The vacuum is also used on carpeted stairs. The red handheld unit is pressed against a gray stair tread between white vertical banister posts, with a polished wooden rail or stair edge visible at the bottom. A hand holds the top handle as the compact vacuum fits into the stair area, where a full-size vacuum would be harder to maneuver. The commercial returns to the living room view. The person again guides the blue upright vacuum over the carpet, then the image shifts back to the red handheld Dirt Devil held at about waist height, visually comparing the small hand vac to the larger upright. The final product display places the red Dirt Devil hand vac on a clean white background. Large red lettering reads “Dirt Devil,” with smaller black text beside it reading “HAND VAC.” The Royal brand name appears below, and the product sits angled to show its red body, rear dust bag, handle, vents, and black front nozzle.

A large yellow-and-white bag labeled “POTATO CHIPS” sits high on an open shelf in a bright white kitchen. Around it are ordinary kitchen items: a blender base and jar to the left, a white pitcher to the right, and, farther out, utensils and cookware. A thin cord or chain hangs down from the shelf area. As the view reveals more of the kitchen, a stocky bulldog appears below, standing on the floor directly under the shelf. The dog is mostly white with brown patches on its face, looking forward with a heavy, slightly droopy expression. A black rectangular sign with large white serif letters appears across the middle of the scene reading “DUMB IDEA,” visually labeling this arrangement of keeping chips up high, with the dog beneath, as a bad solution. Against a plain dark gray studio background, an older white-haired man in black-framed glasses appears holding a box of Orville Redenbacher’s Smart-Pop popcorn beside his face. He wears a bright blue shirt, black suspenders, and a pink patterned bow tie. Smiling, he points a finger to his temple as a white sign above him reads “SMART IDEA.” The product box is cream-colored with green lettering and popcorn imagery, and the large name “SMART-POP” is visible on the front. Back in a sunlit home kitchen, a middle-aged woman with shoulder-length reddish-brown hair and bangs stands behind a wooden counter with an oversized potato chip bag in front of her. She wears a dark long-sleeved top and tan pants. She grips the top of the chip bag, reaches inside, and struggles with it, pulling and twisting the crinkly package as if trying to control or stop herself from eating from it. Her motions become increasingly exaggerated, with the bag pressed against her body and swung around as she wrestles with it. The same black “DUMB IDEA” sign appears across the lower part of the picture while she continues fumbling with the chips. The commercial then presents Orville Redenbacher’s Smart-Pop as a product display. A rectangular Smart-Pop box sits in front of a tall royal-blue popcorn tub overflowing with popped corn. Loose popcorn pieces are scattered across the tabletop. Above the products, a white banner reads “SMART IDEA.” The packaging shows the Orville Redenbacher’s name in a green arch, a small portrait emblem, and the large “SMART-POP” name. A red starburst on the box says “NEW! 80% LESS FAT,” and smaller text along the bottom mentions less fat and fewer calories. In a living-room-like setting, two men sit side by side at a small table with popcorn. On the right is the older Orville Redenbacher spokesperson, again in blue shirt, suspenders, bow tie, and glasses. On the left is a younger adult man with short dark hair, glasses, and a shiny gray striped shirt. A lamp stands behind them. On the table are a blue Smart-Pop popcorn tub filled to the top, a bowl of popcorn, and the Smart-Pop box. Small white on-screen text along the bottom reads “COMPARISON BASED ON WEIGHT.” The younger man gestures as if explaining, then reaches toward the popcorn. The older man smiles and reaches toward the tub too; both men interact casually with the popcorn, sharing the snack and looking pleased. A close view fills the screen with fluffy white popcorn piled high in the blue tub. A hand enters from above and pinches up a piece from the top, then withdraws, leaving the mound of popcorn bright and inviting. The woman from the kitchen is now holding a blue Orville Redenbacher’s Smart-Pop tub full of popcorn. She raises a piece to her mouth and eats it calmly. Her expression softens into a satisfied, guilt-free look as she continues holding the tub close to her chest. A white “SMART IDEA” banner appears across the lower part of the image while she looks forward and reaches for more popcorn. The final product display returns: the Smart-Pop box in front, the blue overflowing tub behind it, and scattered popcorn all around. Beneath the products, large printed text reads, “Do One Thing And Do It Better Than Anyone.” It is signed with the name Orville Redenbacher.

The commercial opens in a warmly lit dining room during a children’s birthday party. Several young children sit around a table covered with plates and clear glasses of red drink. In the center is a decorated birthday cake with a small lit candle, and pink balloons float in the background near a bright window with shutters. A little child with curly blond hair leans close to the cake, facing the candle, while a girl with pigtails sits beside them. Suddenly, as the children react and raise their hands, a burst of tiny cake crumbs, sprinkles, or party debris showers upward and rains down over the curly-haired child’s head and the tabletop. The cake remains in the middle, but the area around it looks messy, with particles falling through the warm light. The scene changes to a close view of a wooden floor under a chair. Small pale crumbs are scattered across the floorboards near a white chair leg. A dark, handheld cordless vacuum with a narrow nozzle is lowered toward the mess. The nozzle glides over the crumbs, drawing them up from the floor in a small, controlled path, reaching close to the chair leg where a larger vacuum would be awkward. A small tan puppy appears next, standing in a softly lit room. It walks toward a blue food bowl placed on a black-and-white checkered kitchen floor. The bowl is heaped with dry dog food, and some pieces spill over the rim. The puppy lies down and begins eating near the bowl. In a closer view, the dry food is piled high, then spills down over the side, creating a scatter of kibble on the floor. A dark DustBuster-style vacuum is shown hanging vertically on a wall-mounted charging bracket. A hand in a coral or pink sleeve reaches in and lifts the compact vacuum away from the holder. Back on the checkered kitchen floor, an adult woman in a loose coral top kneels beside the puppy. She pets the puppy with one hand while holding the cordless vacuum in the other. The puppy keeps eating from the blue bowl, and the woman brings the vacuum nozzle to the spilled kibble, cleaning the small pile beside the bowl without disturbing the dog. The setting then shifts to a bright kitchen or dining area with a baby seated in a high chair. The baby, with very light blond hair, wears a teal shirt under light overalls and smiles happily. On the high-chair tray is a small blue cup filled with snack pieces. A closer view shows the cup full of finger-sized snacks. Some of the snacks are later scattered on the floor nearby. A woman with dark hair pulled back, wearing a white-and-dark striped top and dark pants, crouches on the floor beside the high chair. The baby remains seated to the right, watching from the tray area. The woman uses the same dark handheld vacuum to pick up the scattered snack pieces from the pale floor. She guides the nozzle along the floor in short passes, collecting the small bits near a chair leg and beneath the high chair. As the mess disappears, she looks up toward the baby and smiles. At the end, the vacuum is returned to its wall-mounted holder. The dark, tapered body of the handheld cleaner hangs neatly against a light wall, with the product name visible on the front. Large on-screen text appears across the bottom reading “BLACK & DECKER,” accompanied by the brand’s geometric logo, while a hand steadies the vacuum on the charging bracket.

A sleek white twin-propeller airplane flies head-on over rugged, reddish-brown canyon terrain. Its long, narrow wings stretch wide with upturned tips, and the two propellers blur as they spin. The aircraft passes over rock formations, then over a blue body of water bordered by dry land, and finally appears from below against a clear blue sky, banking so its underside, tail, small oval windows, and red registration markings are visible. The scene shifts to a spacious, warmly lit living room with a soft pink carpet filling the foreground. Sunlight casts long horizontal bands across the carpet. Floral upholstered chairs sit on both sides, with side tables and lamps nearby; a fireplace is on the left, framed pictures hang on the walls, and an open doorway at the back reveals another room and a staircase. Near a bright window, a baby with bare shoulders and a round face is held up by an adult woman with curly light-brown hair. The baby smiles broadly and reaches toward her. The woman faces the baby closely, smiling back. The baby is lifted higher, leaning forward over the woman’s face, both of them framed in soft, glowing light from the window behind them. Back in the living room, a small white ball or soft round object bounces or rolls across the pink carpet, emphasizing the carpet’s surface. The setting changes to a theatrical stage. In the foreground, dark silhouettes of seated audience members are visible. Onstage, under hazy purple and amber lighting, a young woman with long dark hair performs in a vivid magenta and purple dress or wrap with shimmering details. Decorative stage scenery, draped curtains, plants, and ornate painted panels surround her. She walks and turns gracefully, swinging a flowing pink fabric around her body. The fabric fans outward in a wide circle, catching the colored light. In closer views, she faces forward with a composed expression, wearing red earrings and an off-the-shoulder, glossy magenta garment trimmed with gold-like accents. The translucent fabric sweeps across her face and body, then she poses with one arm raised, lit from behind by bright stage lights. The commercial returns to the living room. The white ball rolls across the pink carpet as two boys rush in from the right, playing roughly with hockey sticks. An older boy, wearing a light shirt, jeans, and padded gloves, lunges low across the carpet, stretching toward the ball with a stick. A younger boy in a dark sports-style top with striped sleeves clings to or rides on his back, his mouth open in excitement. The older boy slides forward on his stomach, gloves scraping the carpet, while hockey sticks lie across the foreground. The younger boy keeps hold of him as they tumble and skid together. Other children join the pile, including a small blond child in a blue top, and they roll and scramble on the carpet in a playful heap. As the children continue moving in the background, large bold white letters spelling “BASF” appear centered over the living room scene, filling much of the screen.

A hand in a long-sleeved shirt opens a pale cabinet or closet door by a round white knob. As the door slides aside, a neatly arranged linen shelf appears, filled with soft white towels and pillows. On the shelf is a display of small, rounded pottery air fresheners in front of a box labeled “Country Pottery.” The pieces look like little handmade jars: white on the upper half, colored on the lower half, with small rounded caps. Several color versions are grouped around the package, including warm peach, gray-blue, and tan tones. The package has a floral, country-style design, and the scent name “Country Garden” is visible near the bottom. In a bright bathroom, an adult hand places one of the little pottery jars on a glossy white counter beside a sink. The counter reflects the light, and chrome faucet handles, a soap dish, towels, and a pale bottle sit near a window in the background. The jar has a white upper body, a peach-colored lower body, and a pinkish cap. The hand steadies it, then lets it stand upright near the sink. Another pottery jar is carried to a small polished wooden table. The setting has a homey, decorative feel, with a trailing green plant and a pair of tan leather gloves lying nearby. The hand sets down a tan-bottomed jar near the edge of the table, then withdraws, leaving the small pot as part of the tabletop arrangement. A product display follows against a plain studio-like background. Several pottery jars stand around an open box labeled “Country Pottery.” The central box shows one jar inside and a blue label reading “Soft Powder.” The jars have the same rounded white upper shape but different colored lower halves and caps, including gray-blue, peach, and rose. The packaging uses a large arched blue-and-white “Country Pottery” label. The scene changes to a bedside table. A gold-toned picture frame holds a portrait of a person in a blue dress, and beside it are pale yellow flowers in a slender glass vase, a small brass alarm clock, folded papers, and a white teacup on a saucer. A gray-blue-bottomed Country Pottery jar appears on the tabletop near these personal objects, its small dark cap visible above the white rim. On an ornate mantel or shelf, surrounded by white flowers, framed photos, and decorative containers, a hand wearing a ring and metal wristwatch places another peach-bottomed pottery jar near the front edge. The hand releases it carefully, leaving it centered among the soft cream and white décor. A paper calendar lies on a tabletop, with large printed dates visible, including 16, 23, and 30. A tissue box and scattered papers sit nearby. A hand places a peach-bottomed jar directly over the calendar area, holding it by the small cap, then lets go. The pink cap remains visible on top as the jar stands upright on the calendar page. In a child’s or nursery-like area, plush toys sit on a shelf or tabletop: a pink stuffed rabbit with long ears, a purple teddy bear, a round pastel ball, and small toy figures under a lamp. A hand sets down a gray-blue-bottomed pottery jar in the foreground near a small yellow object and folded papers. Once the hand moves away, the jar remains among the toys and soft pastel decorations. In a warm kitchen setting, a hand carries a wooden tray or board through the foreground while a peach-bottomed pottery jar sits in the background on a windowsill or counter. The commercial opens inside the video game, on a dusty tan racecourse in a desert canyon. Several futuristic hover-motorcycles line up across the track, each with a rider in a helmet and racing suit. Low stone barriers run along both sides, orange canyon walls rise in the background, and a large overhead electronic sign hangs above the track. At first the sign reads “SET” in bright yellow block letters, then changes to “GO!” A white race timer appears in the upper left. The viewpoint sits just behind a green-and-teal hover bike marked with a large number 2, centered in the lane. When the race begins, the other racers surge forward, kicking up pale dust clouds and leaving the number 2 bike behind. Its rear glows red-orange as if powered, but it lags under the “GO!” sign while the pack pulls farther ahead. The scene jumps through different game courses to show the racing variety. On a narrow wooden plank bridge suspended over a deep rocky ravine, several hover bikes crowd together, including a large blue-and-white bike marked number 7 very close in front. The planks stretch in a thin line across the gap, with green terrain beyond the canyon. Then the setting changes to a dramatic, futuristic track at night or twilight. A rider speeds along a steeply banked wall, with a deep blue and purple sky, dark building-like structures, and a white lattice track or framework curving below. The bike appears to cling to the side of a twisting tube-like course before the image returns to the original desert starting stretch, where the number 2 bike is still under the glowing “GO!” sign. More racing clips follow. In a sandy canyon turn, hover bikes slide around a bend and throw up thick splashes of dust or sand; a small rating icon sits in the lower left. A close view shows a rider on a yellow-and-red bike marked number 3, wearing a white helmet with red accents. Another bike sweeps past on the inside of the curve, and a large sandy plume fills the left side of the track as racers disappear around the bend. The action then moves to a bright blue water course near a huge wall of falling water or spray. A red-and-yellow bike marked number 1 flies above the water, then lands and skims forward between orange buoys and industrial-looking structures. Next, the racers are on a snowy mountain track bordered by cliffs and rocks. Several hover bikes carve through the snow, leaving pale tracks and blue-tinted glow beneath them as they bunch together and race under a sign ahead. The commercial returns again to the desert starting area with the number 2 bike still sitting beneath the big yellow “GO!” sign. Suddenly the game’s rider gets off the bike. He is a computer-animated, male-presenting racer in a tight green racing suit with red-orange shoulder pads and accents. A small helmet lies on the ground to his right. He runs straight toward the viewer with an angry, urgent expression, his brows sharply lowered and his mouth set. As he gets closer, his face fills the screen: pale, angular, low-polygon features, short brown hair, heavy dark eyebrows, and a scowling look. The edges of a television screen become visible around him, revealing that he is inside the game on an old-fashioned TV. The real-world setting is a warmly lit living room. An elderly white woman with short white hair sits in a cushioned chair, holding a gray PlayStation controller with both hands. She wears a soft white cardigan over a pink blouse or nightdress and looks intently toward the television, her face calm and slightly puzzled. The TV sits in front of her in a wooden entertainment unit or cabinet, with shelves and small decorative objects around it. On the TV screen, the animated racer’s large face is still glaring outward from the game world as if addressing her directly, while she remains seated and continues holding the controller. The product title then appears on a cloudy, silvery-white background with faint lightning-like streaks. In the center is a dark oval logo with gold text reading “Jet Moto 2.” After the logo, the game image returns briefly to the desert start line: the empty number 2 hover bike sits under the “GO!” sign while the green-suited racer stands beside it, with his helmet still on the ground. He moves near the bike as if urging action. The commercial ends back in the living room with the elderly woman holding the controller in her lap, looking forward with a faintly annoyed or confused expression.

Then a black-and-white image of someone handling money or papers at a counter appears with large blue words “LATE FEES,” which are also covered by the red circle-and-slash symbol. More gameplay appears behind large yellow text reading “UNLIMITED PLAY.” One background is a fighting game with two characters facing each other in an arena, health bars and a timer across the top. Another background shows a flying creature, like a pterodactyl, moving across a game screen. The same little flag-holding mascot appears near the lower left as part of the graphic design. The montage continues into another game with a blue watery background and a character moving along a slanted rope or vine; the “SEGA CHANNEL” logo overlays it and then fills the screen on a bright green-and-yellow graphic background. A price message appears over more game footage. Large hot-pink text reads “LESS THAN $15,” first over a fighting game screen and then over a board-game-like screen with colored squares around the edge. An old, wood-framed television sits in a warm, cluttered attic-like living room with slanted ceilings, shelves, windows, and soft sunlight. On the TV screen, a football game is in progress: a player in a white uniform with a red helmet and the number 88 runs while black-and-silver defenders close in. The ball comes loose as players crowd around him. In the room, a heavyset man in a blue T-shirt over a white long-sleeved shirt, shorts, and a dark cap sits forward in a red leather chair, gripping a football and reacting with his mouth open. Across from him, a man in an orange sweatshirt sits in another chair near a coffee table with snacks and magazines. Between them, a golden retriever lounges in a green leather armchair, head resting on the arm. A third man, wearing a tan jacket and a backward dark cap, moves in the background carrying beer. The golden retriever lifts its head, looks alertly toward the men, opens its mouth as if barking, and sits up in the chair. The man in blue turns toward the dog while still holding the football, and the man in orange leans forward, watching. The man in blue raises his arm, and the room becomes visually chaotic and playful: a football and nearby furniture blur through the foreground as if the living-room action is transforming into the game. A hand in the foreground steadies a pack of white-and-blue Miller Lite cans with gold tops, making the product visible as the scene shifts. The action moves onto a bright green football field in a stadium. Two teams line up, one in white uniforms with orange helmets and the other in black jerseys with silver helmets. Sideline figures, cheerleaders, and yard markers are visible in the background. The golden retriever is now on the field, stretching into a playful bow on the turf, front paws down and rear raised, as if preparing to run a route. Back in the living room, the man in the tan jacket opens or handles a Miller Lite can while the man in orange watches the television. On the TV, the man in blue appears inside the football game, now standing on the field without a helmet among the uniformed players. He crouches near the offensive line as the teams prepare for the snap, while the dog trots behind the formation. The play begins: players surge forward, and the dog runs across the field behind the line. The man in blue, still in his casual shirt and shorts, drops back with the football while large helmeted players block and collide around him. The retriever darts through the action, weaving past running legs and avoiding defenders. The man in blue raises the ball to pass as players in black and silver close in from both sides. The dog sprints downfield, ears flapping and fur shining in the sun. A defender’s legs flash past in the foreground, but the retriever keeps running. The man in blue releases the pass under pressure. Against a vivid blue sky streaked with clouds, the golden retriever leaps high, body stretched out, mouth open around the spinning football. A black-and-silver defender reaches up beneath it, but the dog snatches the ball cleanly in its jaws. The dog lands on the grass and keeps moving with the football in its mouth. A defender reaches toward the dog’s tail, but the retriever slips away and runs low and fast along the field. The football action briefly gives way to a product image: golden beer pours into a tilted glass, filling it with amber liquid and a thick white foamy head. Bubbles stream upward through the beer. Then an amber Miller Lite bottle covered in condensation stands beside a frosty glass mug, with more bottles blurred behind it. The label shows large blue “Lite” lettering, and small white text at the bottom reads “©1995 Miller Brewing Co., Milwaukee WI.” The glass foams over as it is set near the bottle, emphasizing the cold beer. Back on the field, the golden retriever races toward the end zone while defenders chase. A referee raises both arms to signal a score as the dog crosses near the goal line. Stadium walls behind the play display “Lite” signs. A jubilant view follows of the man in blue wedged among helmeted players, grinning broadly, his face and shirt smeared with grass and dirt, with tufts of turf stuck to him. The dog lies on the grass with the football, rolling playfully on its back and pawing at the ball. In the living room, the man in the tan jacket and the man in the orange sweatshirt celebrate, raising their arms and laughing; the man in orange holds a Miller Lite can. The dog then becomes the holder for a kick. On the field, its furry front paws steady a football upright on the turf, and the ball itself has large white “Lite” lettering printed on it. The man in blue runs up to kick while a referee crouches behind the dog. Seen through the yellow goalpost, players crowd the line in the foreground as the man in blue swings his leg and sends the ball upward. A blue banner appears across the bottom of the screen reading “Lite is good.” in white letters, with a round Lite logo at the right. The referee behind the dog raises both arms to signal the kick is good. The final image returns to the living room, where the two seated men continue celebrating in their chairs, lifting their arms and cans while the same “Lite is good.” banner remains across the bottom.

A huge mosquito fills the screen in extreme close-up, far larger than life. Its body is dark and glossy with purplish highlights, covered in bristly hairs, and its large green compound eyes glitter with a dotted texture. Its long needle-like proboscis points forward while its thin legs and translucent wings blur around it against a hazy purple-gray background, making it look as if it is hovering or closing in. The view then cuts to a living room at night or in dim bluish-purple light. A young teenage boy sits centered on a pale couch, facing a large dark television set in the foreground with his hands held low as if using a game controller. Around him are casual household items: a plaid blanket draped over the couch to his right, papers or magazines on the cushions, and furniture and stairs visible in the background. He looks tense and alert, staring toward the television. The mosquito returns in another close-up, now head-on, its two green eyes dominating the image as its proboscis points downward. A brief distorted, kaleidoscopic visual effect repeats the boy’s face and upper body many times in a swirling pattern, as if his anxious gaze and the insect’s threat are being visually mixed together. Back on the couch, the boy turns his eyes sideways with a wary, uneasy expression. The mosquito is then shown in profile perched on human skin, its spindly legs planted among visible fine hairs. Its pale, translucent wings glow at the edges, and its long proboscis presses into the skin as if biting. The commercial switches to video game footage: first a fighting game scene with stone columns, statues, and a blue background, with two characters battling while a rating box marked “MA-13” sits at the lower right and small text along the bottom says that Sega Genesis game screens are shown. One fighter is knocked or thrown across the screen. Then basketball game footage appears in a crowded arena, with players in bright uniforms leaping near the hoop; a “GA” rating box appears at the lower right, and small white game-screen text remains along the bottom. After the game images, the mosquito is shown again on skin in glowing purple light, its abdomen swollen and reddish-orange, implying it has fed. It clings to the skin with long black legs while the proboscis remains near or in the surface. The boy is then seen in a close-up from above, seated on the couch, rolling his eyes upward. A tiny dark mosquito sits directly in the middle of his forehead. A rolled-up newspaper or magazine suddenly rises in front of his face, covering him from forehead to chin. The visible page is a crossword puzzle; red handwritten letters fill the squares to spell “WELCOME TO THE NEXT LEVEL.” The final image is a white background with the word “SEGA” written in thick, smeared dark red letters, surrounded by splatters and streaks like a messy stamped or swatted mark.

In bright outdoor light on a sports field, teenage boys play a rough flag-football-style game in front of empty metal bleachers and trees. A brown-haired teen in a white jersey with blue stripes and the large number 21 reaches up and catches the football while other boys in purple and white jerseys crowd around him. He runs with the ball, but a boy in a purple jersey, number 85, closes in. The play becomes a blur of motion as the boy in white is taken down, sliding onto the green grass. Only legs, shoes, and the edge of his white uniform are visible as he lands on the turf. The scene shifts to a locker room with gray lockers, hanging lights, and several teenage boys changing clothes in the background. From the viewpoint of an open laundry bin or chute, a shirtless teen with wet, tousled hair stands in front holding a bundled white garment. He grins and tosses clothing forward into the opening. Other boys in athletic shorts move around behind him. The white jersey with blue stripes and the number 21 appears among the clothes being handled, suggesting it is the shirt from the field. Back outside, the same teen in the white number 21 jersey presses the fabric up over his nose and face. In close view, he holds the shirt against his face as if smelling or wiping with it. His dark hair falls over his forehead, and the white fabric covers most of his face. The jersey is no longer crisp; it looks worn and dirty, with smudges and grass-colored stains. Back in the locker room, another shirtless teenage boy with curly hair brings a bulky pile of clothes toward the same open laundry bin. He pushes the bundle forward, and the number 21 jersey lies prominently at the front, its blue number visible amid the white fabric. The boy looks down at the shirt as it rests near the opening, while other teammates move in the background among the lockers. The game continues outdoors. The number 21 player reaches up alongside another boy in a white jersey numbered 61 as both stretch for the football. Arms are extended high, and other players watch from nearby. The ball passes through the group, and the number 21 player turns afterward, smiling. His jersey front is visibly stained and dingy, with patches of dirt around the chest and number. Indoors again, a teenage boy wearing a maroon overshirt over a white T-shirt stands by a red duffel bag. He holds the dirty white number 21 jersey, folds or bunches it, and places it into the bright red bag. In close view, the jersey lands inside the open duffel; hands press it down and zip or close the bag around it. In a laundry area at home, a woman with shoulder-length brown hair, wearing a dark plaid shirt tucked into jeans, pulls the number 21 jersey from the red duffel. A man stands just behind her, watching. The jersey is held up between them; the blue number 21 is large on the front, and the white fabric is heavily marked with yellow-green dirt and grass stains, especially around the chest and underarm areas. The woman examines the fabric closely, pinching and lifting sections, while the man peers over her shoulder with a concerned look. On a shelf beside them sits an orange box of Tide with Bleach, its large white “Tide” logo visible against a sunburst background. The woman lowers the dirty jersey back toward the laundry and reaches up toward the shelf. The Tide with Bleach box is then shown close up: an orange package with a bright yellow sunburst pattern, the large white and blue “Tide” name, and the words “with BLEACH” printed beneath it. A hand brings in a blue plastic scoop filled with white powder. The scoop tilts, and the powder pours out in a steady white stream, suggesting detergent being added for the wash. A demonstration follows on a dark surface. A white shirt with two red sleeve stripes lies flat, showing pale greenish stains on the body. Product boxes sit above the shirts: on the left, a red box labeled “Detergent plus Bleach,” and on the right, the orange Tide with Bleach box. A second white shirt with matching red sleeve stripes is placed on the right side for comparison. The left shirt remains visibly dingy and stained, while the right shirt appears cleaner and whiter under the Tide with Bleach package. Near the end, the woman and the teenage boy stand together in a softly lit room with white window blinds and greenery visible outside. She holds up the now-clean white number 21 jersey, and the boy, now in a brown shirt, takes it from her. The jersey looks bright white, with the blue number and sleeve stripes clear. He looks down at it, then bends his head to press his face into the fabric as if checking or savoring its freshness. The woman smiles at him. The final product image places a box of Tide with Bleach beside a neat stack of folded towels in white and pale pink. Across the bottom, white on-screen text reads, “IF IT’S GOT TO BE CLEAN, IT’S GOT TO BE TIDE.”

The commercial opens in a carefully arranged, black-and-white home interior with no people present. She then returns to the floor and presses tile pieces into place along the edge of a cabinet or wall, using her hands to smooth and align them. A rectangular tile is fitted into a corner area, and she adjusts it carefully so it sits flush with the surrounding tiles. A graphic demonstration follows: a stack or layered arrangement of dark marbled vinyl squares is shown against a plain background. Over it, the word “VINYL” repeats vertically in large white letters across the screen, visually stressing that the material is vinyl throughout. The layered tiles overlap like thin sheets, with their marbled pattern visible on the exposed surfaces. As it passes over the tile, it clears away the dark mess, leaving the light square visibly clean behind it. The woman now stands in the kitchen wearing a neat mid-century dress with a fitted waist and full skirt, dark low heels, and styled hair. She mops the checkerboard floor near the white chair and flower-filled desk. The floor looks clean and glossy. She finishes mopping, lifts the mop upright, and steps toward the glass door on the right, carrying the mop with an easy, tidy posture. She exits out of view, leaving the spotless checkerboard kitchen visible. The kitchen fades into a close view of an open telephone directory or classified pages lying on a surface, with a pencil across the page and a rotary telephone behind it. The projected image changes to another child’s picture, and a suited man stands to the right of the screen holding a small wired remote control near his chest. The guests are seated together on the sofa: the two women and a suited man sit close, smiling and looking toward the presenter. The presenter stands beside the small table with the projector on it, holding the wired remote. The lit table lamp glows behind the sofa, and the group appears pleased and engaged at the end of the slide show. One seated man raises a hand or small control toward the standing presenter as they all react to the demonstration. The projector returns on a plain surface for the closing product display. Large white text at the bottom reads, “Only $11.95 Down.” The product remains centered, showing its sloped top, front buttons, and side lens. The image then blends into a circular camera-lens graphic. Around the ring are lens markings including “ANSCO” and “f:2,” with smaller technical lettering around the inner rim. Inside the lens circle, different Ansco products appear one after another: a box labeled “Anscochrome” with the word “ANSCOCHROME” below it, then a box labeled “Ansco” with the on-screen words “All-Weather Pan,” then a simple front view of a camera with the word “CAMERAS.” Finally, the Anscomatic projector appears inside the same lens circle with the word “ANSCOMATIC” beneath it, tying the projector to the broader Ansco camera and film line.
